सर्वं ब्रह्मौपनिषदं माऽहं ब्रह्म निराकुर्यां मा मा ब्रह्म निराकरोदनिराकरणमस्त्वनिराकरणं मेऽस्तु ।
तदात्मनि निरते य उपनिषत्सु धर्मास्ते मयि सन्तु ते मयि सन्तु ॥
iast: oṃ āpyāyantu mamāṅgāni vāk prāṇaś cakṣuḥ śrotram atho balam indriyāṇi ca sarvāṇi
sarvaṃ brahmaupaniṣadaṃ mā'haṃ brahma nirākuryāṃ mā mā brahma nirākarod anirākaraṇam astv anirākaraṇaṃ me'stu
tad ātmani nirate ya upaniṣatsu dharmās te mayi santu te mayi santu

tr.text: Om ! Let my limbs and speech, Prana, eyes, ears, vitality And all the senses grow in strength. All existence is the Brahman of the Upanishads. May I never deny Brahman, nor Brahman deny me. Let there be no denial at all: Let there be no denial at least from me. May the virtues that are proclaimed in the Upanishads be in me, Who am devoted to the Atman; may they reside in me. Om ! Peace ! Peace ! Peace !

sa: ओम् इत्य् एतद् अक्षरम् उद्गीथम् उपासीत ।
iast: om ity etad akṣaram udgītham upāsīta ।

alt.text: Worship ye OM, the eternal syllable. OM is Udgitha, the chant of Samaveda; for with OM they begin the chant of Sama. And this is the exposition of OM.

tr.text: One should meditate on the syllable Om; the Udgitha, for one sings the Udgitha, beginning with Om. Of this, the explanation follows.

alt.text: Earth is the substantial essence of all these creatures and the waters are the essence of earth; herbs of the field are the essence of the waters; man is the essence of the herbs. Speech is the essence of man, Rigveda the essence of Speech, Sama the essence of Rik. Of Sama OM is the essence.

tr.text: The essence of all these beings is the earth. The essence of the earth is water. The essence of water is vegetation. The essence of vegetation is man. The essence of man is speech. The essence of speech is Rik. The essence of Rik is Saman. The essence of Saman is Udgitha.

sa: स एष रसानां रसतमः परमः परार्ध्यो ऽष्टमो यदुद्गीथः ॥
iast: sa eṣa rasānāṃ rasatamaḥ paramaḥ parārdhyo ’ṣṭamo yadudgīthaḥ ॥

alt.text: This is the eighth essence of the essences and the really essential, the highest and it belongeth to the upper hemisphere of things.

tr.text: The syllable Om which is called Udgitha, is the quintessence of the essences, the supreme, deserving of the highest place and the eighth.

sa: कतमा कतम र्क् कतमत् कतमत् साम कतमः कतम उद्गीथ इति विमृष्टं भवति ॥
iast: katamā katama rk katamat katamat sāma katamaḥ katama udgītha iti vimṛṣṭaṃ bhavati ॥

alt.text: Which among things & which again is Rik; which among things and which again is Sama; which among things and which again is OM of the Udgitha — this is now pondered.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise
chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions

tr.text: Which one is Rik ? Which one is Saman ? Which one is Udgitha ? This is being considered now.

sa: तद् वा एतन् मिथुनं यद् वाक् च प्राणश् चर्क् च साम च ॥
iast: tad vā etan mithunaṃ yad vāk ca prāṇaś cark ca sāma ca ॥

alt.text: Speech is Rik, Breath is Sama; the Imperishable is OM of Udgitha. These are the divine lovers, Speech & Breath, Rik & Sama.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise
a word of solemn affirmation and respectful assent
chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Speech alone is Rik. Prana is Saman. The syllable Om is Udgitha. Speech and Prana, (the sources of) Rik and Saman, taken together form a couple.

sa: तद् एतन् मिथुनम् ओम् इत्य् एतस्मिन्न् अक्षरे संसृज्यते ।
यदा वै मिथुनौ समागच्छत आपयतो वै ताव् अन्यो ऽन्यस्य कामम् ॥
iast: tad etan mithunam om ity etasminn akṣare saṃsṛjyate ।
yadā vai mithunau samāgacchata āpayato vai tāv anyo ’nyasya kāmam ॥

alt.text: As a pair of lovers are these and they cling together in OM the eternal syllable; now when the beloved and her lover meet, verily they gratify each the desire of the other.

words: a word of solemn affirmation and respectful assent
to come together (in a friendly or hostile manner)

tr.text: This couple is joined together in the syllable Om. Whenever a couple come together, they, indeed, fulfil each other’s desire.

sa: आपयिता ह वै कामानां भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अक्षरम् उद्गीथम् उपास्ते ॥
iast: āpayitā ha vai kāmānāṃ bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaram udgītham upāste ॥

alt.text: He becometh a gratifier of the desires of men who with this knowledge worshippeth OM the eternal syllable.

words: chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions

tr.text: He who meditates upon this syllable as Udgitha knowing it thus (as the fulfiller), verily becomes a fulfiller of all the desirable ends.

sa: यद् धि किंचानुजानात्य् ओम् इत्य् एव तद् आह ।
समर्धयिता ह वै कामानां भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अक्षरम् उद्गीथम् उपास्ते ॥
iast: yad dhi kiṃcānujānāty om ity eva tad āha ।
samardhayitā ha vai kāmānāṃ bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaram udgītham upāste ॥

alt.text: Now this OM is the syllable of Assent; for to whatsoever one assenteth, one sayeth OM; and assent is blessing of increase. Verily he becometh a blesser and increaser of the desires of men who with this knowledge worshippeth OM the eternal syllable.

words: a word of solemn affirmation and respectful assent
chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions

tr.text: That verily is the syllable of assent, for whenever one assents to a thing, one says only ‘Om’. Assent alone is prosperity. He who meditates upon this syllable as Udgitha, knowing it thus (as endowed with the quality of prosperity), verily becomes one who increases all the desirable ends.

alt.text: By OM the triple knowledge proceedeth; with OM the priest reciteth the Rik, with OM he pronounceth the Yajur, with OM he chanteth the Sama. And all this is for the heaping up of the Imperishable and by the greatness of It and the delightfulness.

tr.text: With this does the threefold knowledge proceed; (because) with Om does one cause to listen; with Om does one recite; with Om does one sing aloud. For the worship of this syllable, with its own greatness and essence (the Vedic rites are performed).

sa: यश् चैतद् एवं वेद यश् च न वेद ।
यद् एव विद्यया करोति श्रद्धयोपनिषदा तद् एव वीर्यवत्तरं भवतीति खल्व् एतस्यैवाक्षरस्योपव्याख्यानं भवति ॥
iast: yaś caitad evaṃ veda yaś ca na veda ।
yad eva vidyayā karoti śraddhayopaniṣadā tad eva vīryavattaraṃ bhavatīti khalv etasyaivākṣarasyopavyākhyānaṃ bhavati ॥

alt.text: He doeth works by OM who hath the knowledge, and he also who hath it not; but these are diverse, the Knowledge and the Ignorance. Whatso work one doeth with knowledge, with faith and with the secret of Veda, it becometh to him more virile and mighty. This is the exposition of the eternal letters.

words: (according to some) the sitting down at the feet of another to listen to his wor

tr.text: He who knows it thus and he who does not know – both perform actions with it. For knowledge and ignorance are different (in their results). Whatever is performed with knowledge, faith and meditation becomes more effective. Up to this truly is the explanation of (the greatness of) this syllable Om.

sa: उभये प्राजापत्यास् तद् ध देवा उद्गीथम् आजह्रुर् अनेनैनान् अभिभविष्याम इति ॥
iast: ubhaye prājāpatyās tad dha devā udgītham ājahrur anenainān abhibhaviṣyāma iti ॥

alt.text: The Gods and the Demons strove together and both were children of the Almighty Father. Then the Gods took up for weapon OM of Udgitha, for they said “With this we shall overcome these Titans.”-

tr.text: Once upon a time the gods and the demons, both descendants of Prajapati, were engaged in a fight. In that fight, the gods performed the rites of the Udgatir priests resolving, ‘With this we shall defeat them’.

sa: ते ह नासिक्यं प्राणम् उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रिरे ।
तस्मात् तेनोभयं जिघ्रति सुरभि च दुर्गन्धि च ।
iast: te ha nāsikyaṃ prāṇam udgītham upāsāṃ cakrire ।
tasmāt tenobhayaṃ jighrati surabhi ca durgandhi ca ।

alt.text: The Gods worshipped OM as Breath in the nostrils; but the Demons came and smote it with the arrow of Evil; therefore it smelleth both alike, the sweet scent and the evil odour. For it is smitten through and through with Evil.

tr.text: Then they meditated on (the deity of) Prana connected with the nose, as Udgitha; the demons pierced it with evil. Therefore with it, the nose, one smells both the fragrant and the foul, for it has been pierced with evil.

sa: अथ ह वाचम् उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रिरे ।
तस्मात् तयोभयं वदति सत्यं चानृतं च ।
iast: atha ha vācam udgītham upāsāṃ cakrire ।
tasmāt tayobhayaṃ vadati satyaṃ cānṛtaṃ ca ।

alt.text: Then the Gods worshipped OM as Speech; but the Demons came and smote it with the arrow of Evil; therefore it speaketh both alike, Truth and Falsehood. For it is smitten through and through with Evil.

words: chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions

tr.text: Then they meditated on (the deity of) speech as Udgitha; the demons pierced it with evil. Therefore with it one speaks both truth and untruth, for it has been pierced with evil.

sa: अथ ह चक्षुर् उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रिरे ।
तस्मात् तेनोभयं पश्यति दर्शनीयं चादर्शनीयं च ।
iast: atha ha cakṣur udgītham upāsāṃ cakrire ।
tasmāt tenobhayaṃ paśyati darśanīyaṃ cādarśanīyaṃ ca ।

alt.text: Then the Gods worshipped OM as the Eye; but the Demons came and smote it with the arrow of Evil; therefore it beholdeth both alike, the fair to see and the foul of favour. For it is smitten through and through with Evil.

tr.text: Then they meditated on (the deity of) eye as Udgitha; the demons pierced it with evil. Therefore with the eye one sees both the sightly and the unsightly, for it has been pierced with evil.

sa: अथ ह श्रोत्रम् उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रिरे ।
तस्मात् तेनोभयं शृणोति श्रवणीयं चाश्रवणीयं च ।
iast: atha ha śrotram udgītham upāsāṃ cakrire ।
tasmāt tenobhayaṃ śṛṇoti śravaṇīyaṃ cāśravaṇīyaṃ ca ।

alt.text: Then the Gods worshipped OM as the Ear; but the Demons came and smote it with the arrow of Evil; therefore it heareth both alike, that which is well to hear and that which is harsh and unseemly. For it is smitten through and through with Evil.

words: chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions

tr.text: Then they meditated on (the deity of) ear as Udgitha; the demons pierced it with evil. Therefore with the ear one hears both the pleasant and the unpleasant, for it has been pierced with evil.

sa: अथ ह मन उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रिरे ।
iast: atha ha mana udgītham upāsāṃ cakrire ।

alt.text: Then the Gods worshipped Udgitha as Mind; but the Demons came and smote it with the arrow of Evil; therefore it conceiveth both alike, right thoughts and unlawful imaginations. For it is smitten through and through with Evil.

tr.text: Then they meditated on (the deity of) mind as Udgitha; the demons pierced it with evil. Therefore with the mind one thinks both good and evil thoughts, for it has been pierced with evil.

sa: अथ ह य एवायं मुख्यः प्राणस् तम् उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रिरे ।
तं हासुरा ऋत्वा विदध्वंसुर् यथाश्मानम् आखणम् ऋत्वा विध्वंसेतैवम् ॥
iast: atha ha ya evāyaṃ mukhyaḥ prāṇas tam udgītham upāsāṃ cakrire ।
taṃ hāsurā ṛtvā vidadhvaṃsur yathāśmānam ākhaṇam ṛtvā vidhvaṃsetaivam ॥

alt.text: Then the Gods worshipped OM as this which is Breath in the mouth and the Demons rushing against it dashed themselves to pieces; as when an object striketh against firm and solid rock, it dasheth to pieces upon the rock.

tr.text: Then they meditated on the Prana in the mouth as Udgitha. The demons came in clash with it and were destroyed, just as a lump of clay is destroyed, striking against a hard rock.

sa: एवं यथाश्मानम् आखणम् ऋत्वा विध्वंसत एवं हैव स विध्वंसते य एवंविदि पापं कामयते यश् चैनम् अभिदासति ।
iast: evaṃ yathāśmānam ākhaṇam ṛtvā vidhvaṃsata evaṃ haiva sa vidhvaṃsate ya evaṃvidi pāpaṃ kāmayate yaś cainam abhidāsati ।

alt.text: And even as an object hurling against firm and solid rock dasheth itself to pieces, so he hurleth himself upon destruction whoso desireth evil against the Knower or whoso doeth him hurt; for the Knower is as that firm and solid rock.

tr.text: Thus it is that the Prana in the mouth has not been destroyed and is pure. Even as a lump of clay striking against a hard rock is destroyed, so will he be destroyed who wishes to do evil to one who knows this (the purity of Prana) or who (actually) injures that knower, for he is like a hard rock.

sa: तेन यद् अश्नाति यत् पिबति तेनेतरान् प्राणान् अवति ।
iast: tena yad aśnāti yat pibati tenetarān prāṇān avati ।

alt.text: With this Breath one cogniseth neither sweet scent nor ill odour, for it hath flung Evil from it. Whatsoever one eateth with this or drinketh, thereby it cherisheth the other breaths. At the end and last when he findeth not the breath, the Spirit goeth out from the body; verily he openeth wide the mouth as he goeth.

tr.text: With this Prana in the mouth one discerns neither sweet smell nor foul, for it is free from sin. What one eats or drinks through this, even with that he maintains the other Pranas. And not finding this at the time of death, the Prana in the mouth and its dependants depart; and thus indeed one opens the mouth at the time of death.

sa: एतम् उ एवाङ्गिरसं मन्यन्ते ऽङ्गानां यद् रसः ॥
iast: etam u evāṅgirasaṃ manyante ’ṅgānāṃ yad rasaḥ ॥

alt.text: Angiras worshipped OM of Udgitha as Breath in the mouth and men think of Breath in the mouth as Angiras because it is essence of the members of the body.

tr.text: Angiras meditated on that Prana as Udgitha. The sages consider this alone as Angirasa which is the essence of the limbs.

sa: तेन तं ह बृहस्पतिर् उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रे ।
iast: tena taṃ ha bṛhaspatir udgītham upāsāṃ cakre ।

alt.text: By the strength of Angiras, Brihaspati worshipped OM as Breath in the mouth, and men think of the Breath as Brihaspati, because Speech is the great goddess and Breath is the lord of Speech.

tr.text: So Brihaspati meditated on Prana as Udgitha. The sages consider this alone as Brihaspati, for speech is great and this Prana is its lord.

sa: तेन तं हायास्य उद्गीथम् उपासां चक्रे ।
iast: tena taṃ hāyāsya udgītham upāsāṃ cakre ।

alt.text: By the strength of Brihaspati, Ayasya worshipped OM as Breath in the mouth and men think of the Breath as Ayasya, because ’tis from the mouth it cometh.

tr.text: So Ayasya meditated on Prana as Udgitha (identifying it with himself). The sages consider this alone as Ayasya for it goes out of the mouth.

sa: तेन तं ह बको दाल्भ्यो विदां चकार ।
iast: tena taṃ ha bako dālbhyo vidāṃ cakāra ।

alt.text: By the strength of Ayasya, Baka the son of Dalbha knew the Breath. And he became the Chanter of the Sama among the Naimishiyas and he chanteth their desires for them unto fulfilment.

tr.text: Baka, the son of Dalbha, knew it thus. So he became the Udgatir-singer of the sacrificers dwelling in Naimisa. For their sake he sang to fulfil their desires.

sa: आगाता ह वै कामानां भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अक्षरम् उद्गीथम् उपास्ते ।
iast: āgātā ha vai kāmānāṃ bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaram udgītham upāste ।

alt.text: Verily he becometh a chanter unto fulfilment of the desires of men who with this knowledge worshippeth OM of Udgitha, the eternal syllable. Thus far concerning Self is the exposition.

tr.text: He who knows it thus and meditates on the Udgitha as the syllable Om, looking upon it as Prana, certainly becomes the singer (and procurer) of the desired objects. This is the meditation with reference to the body.

sa: य एवासौ तपति तम् उद्गीथम् उपासीत ।
अपहन्ता ह वै भयस्य तमसो भवति य एवं वेद ॥
iast: ya evāsau tapati tam udgītham upāsīta ।
apahantā ha vai bhayasya tamaso bhavati ya evaṃ veda ॥

alt.text: Thereafter concerning the Gods. Lo yonder burning fire in the heavens, worship ye Him as the Udgitha; for the Sun riseth & singeth his bright hymn unto the peoples. Yea he riseth, & darkness is slain & its terror — therefore shall he be a slayer of the terror & the darkness, he who thus knoweth.

tr.text: Now the meditation (on the Udgitha) with reference to the gods is described. One should meditate on him who gives heat (i.e. the sun) as Udgitha. Verily, when he rises, he sings aloud for the sake of all creatures. When he rises, he dispels darkness and fear. Verily, he who knows the sun as being endowed with these qualities, becomes the dispeller of darkness and (the consequent) fear.

sa: स्वर इतीमम् आचक्षते स्वर इति प्रत्यास्वर इत्य् अमुम् ।
तस्माद् वा एतम् इमम् अमुं च उद्गीथम् उपासीत ॥
iast: svara itīmam ācakṣate svara iti pratyāsvara ity amum ।
tasmād vā etam imam amuṃ ca udgītham upāsīta ॥

alt.text: Breath & the Sun are one & alike — for the one is heat & the other is heat, and they call Breath the mover and the Sun too they call the mover & they call him also the mover that returneth upon his paths — therefore ye shall worship both the one & the other as Udgitha.

tr.text: This Prana in the mouth and that sun are the same. This is warm and that is warm. People call this as Svara (that is going) and that as Svara and Pratyasvara (that is going and coming). Therefore one should meditate on this Prana and that sun as Udgitha.

sa: अथ यः प्राणापानयोः संधिः स व्यानः ।
iast: atha yaḥ prāṇāpānayoḥ saṃdhiḥ sa vyānaḥ ।

alt.text: Thereafter verily ye shall worship Vyana the middle breath as Udgitha. For when one breathes forth it is Prana, the Main Breath, & when one breathes down it is Apana, the lower breath. Now this which is the joint & linking of the main breath & the lower breath, is Vyana — & Vyana, it is Speech. Therefore ’tis when one neither breatheth forth nor breatheth down that one giveth utterance to Speech.

tr.text: Now, verily one should meditate on Vyana as Udgitha. That which one breathes out is Prana and that which one breathes in is Apana. The junction of Prana and Apana is Vyana. That which is Vyana, even that is speech. Therefore, one utters speech while one neither breathes out nor breathes in.

alt.text: But Speech is the Rik — therefore ’tis when one neither breatheth out nor breatheth in that one uttereth the Rik. And Rik it is Sama — therefore ’tis when one neither breatheth out nor breatheth in that one chanteth the Sama. But Sama it is Udgitha — therefore ’tis when one neither breatheth out nor breatheth in that one singeth Udgitha.

tr.text: That which is speech, even that is Rik. Therefore while one neither breathes out nor breathes in, one pronounces the Rik. That which is Rik, even that is Saman. Therefore, while one neither breathes out nor breathes in, one sings the Saman. That which is Saman, even that is Udgitha. Therefore, while one neither breathes out nor breathes in, one sings the Udgitha.

sa: अतो यान्य् अन्यानि वीर्यवन्ति कर्माणि यथाग्नेर् मन्थनम् आजेः सरणं दृढस्य धनुष आयमनम् अप्राणन्न् अनपानंस् तानि करोति ।
iast: ato yāny anyāni vīryavanti karmāṇi yathāgner manthanam ājeḥ saraṇaṃ dṛḍhasya dhanuṣa āyamanam aprāṇann anapānaṃs tāni karoti ।

alt.text: Hence whatsoever actions there be that are of might & forcefulness as smiting out fire from the tinder or leaping a great barrier or bending a stark & mighty bow, it is when one neither breatheth out nor breatheth in that one doeth these. And for this cause ye shall worship the middle breath as Udgitha.

tr.text: Therefore whatever other actions require strength, such as the kindling of fire by friction, running a race towards a goal, the bending of a strong bow, are all performed, while one neither breathes out nor breathes in. For this reason one should meditate on Vyana as Udgitha.

alt.text: Thereafter verily ye shall worship the syllables of the Udgitha saying Udgitha & Prana is the first syllable, because one riseth up with the main breath & Speech is the second syllable, because they call Speech that which goeth forth & food is the third syllable, because in food all this Universe is established.

tr.text: Now, one should meditate on the syllables of ‘Udgitha’ – namely, the syllables ‘ut’, ‘gi’ and ‘tha’. Prana is ‘ut’, because through Prana one arises (ut-tisthati). Speech is ‘gi’, because speech is called word (girah). Food is ‘tha’, because upon food all this is established (sthitam).

sa: दुग्धे ऽस्मै वाग् दोहं यो वाचो दोहः ।
य एतान्य् एवं विद्वान् उद्गीथाक्षराण्य् उपास्त उद्-गी-थ इति ॥
iast: dugdhe ’smai vāg dohaṃ yo vāco dohaḥ ।
ya etāny evaṃ vidvān udgīthākṣarāṇy upāsta ud-gī-tha iti ॥

alt.text: Heaven is the first syllable, the middle air is the second syllable, earth is the third syllable. The Sun is the first syllable, Air is the second syllable, Fire is the third syllable. The Samaveda is the first syllable, Yajurveda is the second syllable, Rigveda is the third syllable. To him Speech is a cow that yieldeth sweet milk — & what is this milking of Speech? — even that he becometh rich in food & the eater of food who knoweth these & worshippeth the syllables of Udgitha saying lo even this is Udgitha.

tr.text: Heaven is ut, the sky is gi, the earth is tha. The sun is ut, the air gi, the fire, tha. The Sama-Veda is ut, the Yajur-Veda gi, the Rig-Veda tha. For him, speech yields the milk which is the benefit of speech. And he becomes rich in food; and an eater of food, who knows thus and meditates on the syllables of ‘Udgitha’, namely, ut, gi and tha.

sa: येन साम्ना स्तोष्यन् स्यात् तत् सामोपधावेत् ॥
iast: yena sāmnā stoṣyan syāt tat sāmopadhāvet ॥

tr.text: Now follows the fulfilment of wishes: One should meditate on the objects contemplated. One should reflect upon Saman by means of which one proceeds to sing the Stotra.

sa: यस्याम् ऋचि ताम् ऋचं, यद् आर्षेयं तम् ऋषिं, यां देवताम् अभिष्टोष्यन् स्यात् तां देवताम् उपधावेत् ॥
iast: yasyām ṛci tām ṛcaṃ, yad ārṣeyaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ, yāṃ devatām abhiṣṭoṣyan syāt tāṃ devatām upadhāvet ॥

tr.text: One should reflect upon the Rik in which that Saman occurs, upon the sage by whom it is intuited and upon the deity to whom he proceeds to pray.

sa: येन च्छन्दसा स्तोष्यन् स्यात् तच् छन्द उपधावेत् ।
येन स्तोमेन स्तोष्यमाणः स्यात् तं स्तोमम् उपधावेत् ॥
iast: yena cchandasā stoṣyan syāt tac chanda upadhāvet ।
yena stomena stoṣyamāṇaḥ syāt taṃ stomam upadhāvet ॥

tr.text: One should reflect upon the metre in which he proceeds to sing a Stotra; and he should reflect upon the hymn with which he proceeds to sing it.

sa: यां दिशम् अभिष्टोष्यन् स्यात् तां दिशम् उपधावेत् ॥
iast: yāṃ diśam abhiṣṭoṣyan syāt tāṃ diśam upadhāvet ॥

tr.text: He should reflect upon the quarter (of heaven) towards which he proceeds to sing a Stotra.

sa: आत्मानम् अन्तत उपसृत्य स्तुवीत कामं ध्यायन्न् अप्रमत्तः ।
अभ्याशो ह यद् अस्मै स कामः स्मृध्येत यत्कामः स्तुवीतेति यत्कामः स्तुवीतेति ॥
iast: ātmānam antata upasṛtya stuvīta kāmaṃ dhyāyann apramattaḥ ।
abhyāśo ha yad asmai sa kāmaḥ smṛdhyeta yatkāmaḥ stuvīteti yatkāmaḥ stuvīteti ॥

tr.text: Lastly, having thought about himself, he should sing a Stotra reflecting upon his desired object avoiding all faults. Very quickly will be fulfilled for him the desire, desiring which he may sing the Stotra yea, desiring which he may sing the Stotra.

sa: ओम् इत्य् एतद् अक्षरम् उद्गीथम् उपासीत ।
iast: om ity etad akṣaram udgītham upāsīta ।
words: a word of solemn affirmation and respectful assent
chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions

tr.text: One should meditate on the syllable Om, the Udgitha, for one sings the Udgitha beginning with Om. Of this the explanation follows.

sa: देवा वै मृत्योर् बिभ्यतस् त्रयीं विद्यां प्राविशन् ।
यद् एभिर् अच्छादयंस् तच् छन्दसां छन्दस्त्वम् ॥
iast: devā vai mṛtyor bibhyatas trayīṃ vidyāṃ prāviśan ।
yad ebhir acchādayaṃs tac chandasāṃ chandastvam ॥

tr.text: Verily, the gods, being afraid of death, took refuge in the three Vedas. They covered themselves with the metrical hymns. Because they covered themselves with these, the metrical hymns are called Chandas.

sa: तान् उ तत्र मृत्युर् यथा मत्स्यम् उदके परिपश्येद् एवं पर्यपश्यद् ऋचि साम्नि यजुषि ।
ते नु वित्त्वोर्ध्वा ऋचः साम्नो यजुषः स्वरम् एव प्राविशन् ॥
iast: tān u tatra mṛtyur yathā matsyam udake paripaśyed evaṃ paryapaśyad ṛci sāmni yajuṣi ।
te nu vittvordhvā ṛcaḥ sāmno yajuṣaḥ svaram eva prāviśan ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Just as a fisherman would see a fish in water, so did Death observe the gods in the (rites connected with) Rik, Saman and Yajus. They, too, knowing this, arose from the Rik, Saman and Yajus, and entered the Svara (the syllable Om).

sa: यदा वा ऋचम् आप्नोत्य् ओम् इत्य् एवातिस्वरति एवं सामैवं यजुः ।
एष उ स्वरो यद् एतद् अक्षरम् एतद् अमृतम् अभयम् ।
iast: yadā vā ṛcam āpnoty om ity evātisvarati evaṃ sāmaivaṃ yajuḥ ।
eṣa u svaro yad etad akṣaram etad amṛtam abhayam ।
words: a word of solemn affirmation and respectful assent
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Verily, when one learns the Rik, he loudly pronounces ‘Om’. It is the same with Saman and with Yajus. This syllable Om is indeed Svara; it again is immortality and fearlessness. Having entered into Svara (i.e. having meditated) the gods became immortal and fearless.

sa: स य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अक्षरं प्रणौत्य् एतद् एवाक्षरं स्वरम् अमृतम् अभयं प्रविशति ।
तत् प्रविश्य यद् अमृता देवास् तद् अमृतो भवति ॥
iast: sa ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaraṃ praṇauty etad evākṣaraṃ svaram amṛtam abhayaṃ praviśati ।
tat praviśya yad amṛtā devās tad amṛto bhavati ॥

tr.text: He who worships this syllable knowing it thus, enters this syllable, the Svara, which is immortality and fearlessness. And having entered it, he becomes immortal by that nectar, by which the gods became immortal.

sa: अथ खलु य उद्गीथः स प्रणवो यः प्रणवः स उद्गीथ इति ।
असौ वा आदित्य उद्गीथ एष प्रणवः ।
ओम् इति ह्य् एष स्वरन्न् एति ॥
iast: atha khalu ya udgīthaḥ sa praṇavo yaḥ praṇavaḥ sa udgītha iti ।
asau vā āditya udgītha eṣa praṇavaḥ ।
om iti hy eṣa svarann eti ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions
a kind of small drum or tabor

tr.text: Now, that which is Udgitha is verily Pranava and that which is Pranava is Udgitha. The yonder sun is Udgitha and also Pranava, for he moves along pronouncing ‘Om’.

sa: एतम् उ एवाहम् अभ्यगासिषं तस्मान् मम त्वम् एको ऽसीति ह कौषीतकिः पुत्रम् उवाच ।
iast: etam u evāham abhyagāsiṣaṃ tasmān mama tvam eko ’sīti ha kauṣītakiḥ putram uvāca ।

tr.text: ‘To him (the sun itself) I sung; therefore you are my only son’ thus said Kausitaki to his son. ‘Reflect upon the Udgitha as the rays of the sun, then surely, you will have many sons. This is the meditation with reference to the gods.

sa: य एवायं मुख्यः प्राणस् तम् उद्गीथम् उपासित ।
ओम् इति ह्य् एष स्वरन्न् एति ॥
iast: ya evāyaṃ mukhyaḥ prāṇas tam udgītham upāsita ।
om iti hy eṣa svarann eti ॥

tr.text: Now (is the meditation) with reference to the body: One should meditate on him who is this Prana in the mouth, as Udgitha, for he moves along pronouncing ‘Om’.

sa: एतम् उ एवाहम् अभ्यगासिषं तस्मान् मम त्वम् एको ऽसीति ह कौषीतकिः पुत्रम् उवाच ।
प्राणांस् त्वं भूमानम् अभिगायताद् बहवो वै मे भविष्यन्तीति ॥
iast: etam u evāham abhyagāsiṣaṃ tasmān mama tvam eko ’sīti ha kauṣītakiḥ putram uvāca ।
prāṇāṃs tvaṃ bhūmānam abhigāyatād bahavo vai me bhaviṣyantīti ॥

tr.text: ‘To him (the Prana itself) did I sing; therefore you are my only son’, thus said Kausitaki to his son. "I shall get many sons", thinking thus, sing praise to the Udgitha as the manifold Pranas.’

sa: अथ खलु य उद्गीथः स प्रणवो यः प्रणवः स उद्गीथ इति ।
होतृषदनाद् ध एवापि दुरुद्गीथम् अनुसमाहरतीत्य् अनुसमाहरतीति ॥
iast: atha khalu ya udgīthaḥ sa praṇavo yaḥ praṇavaḥ sa udgītha iti ।
hotṛṣadanād dha evāpi durudgītham anusamāharatīty anusamāharatīti ॥
