tr.text: ‘Now, that which is Udgitha, is verily Pranava; and that which is Pranava, is Udgitha’, so one should think. As a result of it, even if he chants wrongly, he rectifies it by the act done from the seat of the Hotr priest.

sa: तद् एतद् एतस्याम् ऋच्य् अध्यूढं साम ।
iast: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma ।

tr.text: The earth is Rik, the fire is Saman. This Saman rests upon that Rik. Therefore the Saman is sung as resting upon the Rik. The earth is ‘sa’, the fire is ‘ama’, and that makes ‘Sama’.

sa: तद् एतद् एतस्याम् ऋच्य् अध्यूढं साम ।
iast: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma ।

tr.text: The sky is Rik, the air is Sama. This Saman rests upon that Rik. Therefore the Saman is sung as resting upon the Rik. The sky is ‘sa’, the air is ‘ama’, and that makes ‘Sama’.

sa: तद् एतद् एतस्याम् ऋच्य् अध्यूढं साम ।
iast: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma ।

tr.text: Heaven is Rik, the sun is Saman. This Saman rests upon that Rik. Therefore the Saman is sung as resting upon the Rik. Heaven is ‘sa’, the sun is ‘ama’, and that makes ‘Sama’.

sa: तद् एतद् एतस्याम् ऋच्य् अध्यूढं साम ।
iast: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma ।

tr.text: The stars are Rik, the moon is Saman. This Saman rests upon that Rik. Therefore the Saman is sung as resting upon the Rik. The stars are ‘sa’, the moon is ‘ama’, and that makes ‘Sama’.

sa: अथ यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य शुक्लं भाः सैवर्क् ।
अथ यन् नीलं परःकृष्णं तत् साम ।
तद् एतद् एतस्याम् ऋच्य् अध्यूढं साम ।
iast: atha yad etad ādityasya śuklaṃ bhāḥ saivark ।
atha yan nīlaṃ paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ tat sāma ।
tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma ।

tr.text: Now, the while light of the sun is Rik, the blue (light) that is extremely dark is Saman. This Saman rests upon that Rik. Therefore the Saman is sung as resting upon the Rik.

sa: अथ यद् एवैतद् आदित्यस्य शुक्लं भाः सैव सा ।
अथ यन् नीलं परःकृष्णं तद् अमः ।
अथ य एषो ऽन्तरादित्ये हिरण्मयः पुरुषो दृश्यते हिरण्यश्मश्रुर् हिरण्यकेश आ प्रणखात् सर्व एव सुवर्नः ॥
iast: atha yad evaitad ādityasya śuklaṃ bhāḥ saiva sā ।
atha yan nīlaṃ paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ tad amaḥ ।
atha ya eṣo ’ntarāditye hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣo dṛśyate hiraṇyaśmaśrur hiraṇyakeśa ā praṇakhāt sarva eva suvarnaḥ ॥

tr.text: Again, the white light of the sun is ‘sa’, the blue (light) that is extremely dark is ‘ama’, and that makes ‘Sama’. Now, that Person, effulgent as gold, who is seen within the sun, who is with golden beard and golden hair, is exceedingly effulgent even to the very tips of his nails.

sa: तस्य यथा कप्यासं पुण्डरीकम् एवम् अक्षिणी ।
उदेति ह वै सर्वेभ्यः पाप्मभ्यो य एवं वेद ॥
iast: tasya yathā kapyāsaṃ puṇḍarīkam evam akṣiṇī ।
udeti ha vai sarvebhyaḥ pāpmabhyo ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: His eyes are bright like a red lotus. His name is ‘ut’. He has risen above all evils. Verily, he who knows thus rises above all evils.

sa: स एष ये चामुष्मात् पराञ्चो लोकास् तेषां चेष्ट देवकामानां च ।
iast: sa eṣa ye cāmuṣmāt parāñco lokās teṣāṃ ceṣṭa devakāmānāṃ ca ।

tr.text: Rik and Saman are his two joints. Therefore he is Udgitha. Because the priest is the singer of this ‘ut’, he is the Udgitha. Moreover, he (this Person called ‘ut’) controls the worlds which are above that sun, as also the desires of the gods. This is with reference to the gods.

sa: तद् एतद् एतस्याम् ऋच्य् अध्यूढं साम ।
iast: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma ।

tr.text: Now (is the meditation) with reference to the body: Speech is Rik, Prana is Sama. This Saman rests upon that Rik. Therefore the Saman is sung as resting upon the Rik. Speech is ‘sa’, Prana is ‘ama’ and that makes ‘Sama’.

sa: तद् एतद् एतस्याम् ऋच्य् अध्यूढं साम ।
iast: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma ।

tr.text: The eye is Rik, the self (reflected in the eye) is Saman. This Saman rests upon that Rik. Therefore the Saman is sung as resting upon the Rik. The eye is ‘sa’, the self is ‘ama’, and that makes ‘Sama’.

sa: तद् एतद् एतस्याम् ऋच्य् अध्यूढं साम ।
iast: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma ।

tr.text: The ear is Rik, the mind is Saman. This Saman rests upon that Rik. Therefore the Saman is sung as resting upon the Rik. The ear is ‘sa’, the mind is ‘ama’, and that makes "Sama’.

sa: अथ यद् एतद् अक्ष्नः शुक्लं भाः सैवर्क् ।
अथ यन् नीलं परःकृष्णं तत् साम ।
तद् एतद् एतस्याम् ऋच्य् अध्यूढं साम ।
अथ यद् एवैतद् अक्ष्णः शुक्लं भाः सैव सा ।
अथ यन् नीलं परःकृष्णं तद् अमः ।
iast: atha yad etad akṣnaḥ śuklaṃ bhāḥ saivark ।
atha yan nīlaṃ paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ tat sāma ।
tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma ।
atha yad evaitad akṣṇaḥ śuklaṃ bhāḥ saiva sā ।
atha yan nīlaṃ paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ tad amaḥ ।

tr.text: Now, the white light of the eye is Rik, the blue (light) that is extremely dark is Saman. This Saman rests upon that Rik. Therefore the Saman is sung as resting upon the Rik. The white light of the eye is ‘sa’, the blue (light) that is extremely dark is ‘ama’ and that makes ‘Sama’.

sa: अथ य एषो ऽन्तर् अक्षिणि पुरुषो दृश्यते सैवर्क् ।
तस्य एतस्य तद् एव रूपं यद् अमुष्य रूपम् ।
याव् अमुष्य गेष्णौ तौ तौ गोष्णौ ।
iast: atha ya eṣo ’ntar akṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate saivark ।
tasya etasya tad eva rūpaṃ yad amuṣya rūpam ।
yāv amuṣya geṣṇau tau tau goṣṇau ।

tr.text: Now, this person who is seen within the eye – he indeed is Rik, he is Saman, he is Uktha, he is Yajus, he is the Vedas. The form of this (person seen in the eye) is the same as the form of that (person seen in the sun). His joints are the same as those of the other; his name is the same as that of the other.

sa: स एष ये चैतस्माद् अर्वाञ्चो लोकास् तेषां चेष्टे मनुष्यकामानां चेति ।
तद् य इमे वीणायां गायन्त्य् एतं ते गायन्ति ।
iast: sa eṣa ye caitasmād arvāñco lokās teṣāṃ ceṣṭe manuṣyakāmānāṃ ceti ।
tad ya ime vīṇāyāṃ gāyanty etaṃ te gāyanti ।

tr.text: That (person in the eye) is the lord of all the worlds that are extended below, as also of the desired objects of men. So those who sing on the lute, sing of him alone and thereby become endowed with wealth.

sa: अथ य एतद् एवं विद्वान् साम गायत्य् उभौ स गायति ।
सो ऽमुनैव स एष ये चामुष्मात् पराञ्चो लोकास् तांश् चाप्नोति देवकामांश् च ॥
iast: atha ya etad evaṃ vidvān sāma gāyaty ubhau sa gāyati ।
so ’munaiva sa eṣa ye cāmuṣmāt parāñco lokās tāṃś cāpnoti devakāmāṃś ca ॥

tr.text: Now he who sings the Saman after knowing the deity Udgitha thus, sings to both. Through that (person in the sun), he (that singer) gets the worlds beyond that sun and also the desired objects of gods.

sa: अथानेनैव ये चैतस्माद् अर्वाञ्चो लोकास् तांश् चाप्नोति मनुष्यकामांश् च ।
iast: athānenaiva ye caitasmād arvāñco lokās tāṃś cāpnoti manuṣyakāmāṃś ca ।

tr.text: Similarly, through this person in the eye, one gets the worlds that are extended below this person, and also the desired objects of men. For this reason, the Udgatir priest who knows thus should ask (the sacrificer): ‘What desire shall I obtain for you by singing the Saman ?’ For he alone becomes capable of obtaining desires by singing , who knowing thus sings the Saman – yea, sings the Saman.

sa: एष ह्य् एव कामागानस्येष्टे य एवं विद्वान् साम गायति साम गायति ॥
iast: eṣa hy eva kāmāgānasyeṣṭe ya evaṃ vidvān sāma gāyati sāma gāyati ॥

tr.text: Similarly, through this person in the eye, one gets the worlds that are extended below this person, and also the desired objects of men. For this reason, the Udgatir priest who knows thus should ask (the sacrificer): ‘What desire shall I obtain for you by singing the Saman ?’ For he alone becomes capable of obtaining desires by singing , who knowing thus sings the Saman – yea, sings the Saman.

sa: त्रयो होद्गीथे कुशला बभूवुः शिलकः शालावत्यश् चैकितायनो दाल्भ्यः प्रवाहणो जैवलिर् इति ।
ते होचुर् उद्गीथे वै कुशलाः स्मो हन्तोद्गीथे कथां वदाम इति ॥
iast: trayo hodgīthe kuśalā babhūvuḥ śilakaḥ śālāvatyaś caikitāyano dālbhyaḥ pravāhaṇo jaivalir iti ।
te hocur udgīthe vai kuśalāḥ smo hantodgīthe kathāṃ vadāma iti ॥

tr.text: In ancient times there were three proficient in Udgitha: Silaka the son of Salavat, Caikitayana of the Dalbhya family and Pravahana the son of Jivala. They said, ‘We are proficient in Udgitha. If you agree, let us enter on a discussion of Udgitha’.
‘Let it be so’, saying this they sat down. Then Pravahana Jaivali said, ‘You two, revered sirs, speak first; and I shall listen to the words of two Brahmanas conversing’.

sa: स ह शिलकः शालावत्यश् चैकितायनं दाल्भ्यम् उवाच हन्त त्वा पृच्छानीति ।
iast: sa ha śilakaḥ śālāvatyaś caikitāyanaṃ dālbhyam uvāca hanta tvā pṛcchānīti ।

tr.text: Then Silaka Salavatya said to Caikitayana Dalbhya, ‘If you permit, I shall question you’. ‘Question’, said he.

(Silaka asked), ‘What is the essence of Saman ?’ ‘The tune’, said (Dalbhya). ‘What is the essence of the tune ?’ ‘Prana’, said (Dalbhya). ‘What is the essence of Prana ?’ ‘Food’, said (Dalbhya). ‘What is the essence of food ?’ ‘Water’, said (Dalbhya).

sa: न स्वर्गं लोकम् अतिनयेद् इति होवाच ।
iast: na svargaṃ lokam atinayed iti hovāca ।

tr.text: ‘What is the essence of water ?’ ‘That (heavenly world)’, said (Dalbhya). ‘What is the essence of the world ?’ ‘One cannot carry (the Saman) beyond the heavenly world’, said Dalbhya; ‘we locate the Saman in the world of heaven, for Saman is praised as heaven’.

sa: तं ह शिलकः शालावत्यश् चैकितायनं दाल्भ्यम् उवाचाप्रतिष्ठितं वै किल ते दाल्भ्य साम ।
यस् त्व् एतर्हि ब्रूयान् मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति मूर्धा ते विपतेद् इति ॥
iast: taṃ ha śilakaḥ śālāvatyaś caikitāyanaṃ dālbhyam uvācāpratiṣṭhitaṃ vai kila te dālbhya sāma ।
yas tv etarhi brūyān mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mūrdhā te vipated iti ॥

tr.text: Then Silaka Salavatya said to Caikitayana Dalbhya: ‘O Dalbhya, your Saman is not indeed established. If someone one were to say, "Your head shall fall down", surely your head would fall down’.

sa: न प्रतिष्ठां लोकम् अतिनयेद् इति होवाच ।
iast: na pratiṣṭhāṃ lokam atinayed iti hovāca ।

tr.text: (Dalbhya) ‘Will you permit me, sir, to learn this of you ?’ ‘Learn’, said (Silaka). ‘What is the essence of that (heavenly) world ?’ ‘This earth’, said (Silaka), ‘What is the essence of this earth ?’ ‘One cannot carry the Saman beyond this world as its support’, said Silaka; ‘we locate the Saman in this world as its support, for Saman is extolled as the earth’.

sa: अन्तवद् वै किल ते शालावत्य साम ।
यस् त्व् एतर्हि ब्रूयान् मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति मूर्धा ते विपतेद् इति ।
iast: antavad vai kila te śālāvatya sāma ।
yas tv etarhi brūyān mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mūrdhā te vipated iti ।

tr.text: Pravahana Jaivali said to him, ‘O Salavatya, your Sama, really, has a further end. If someone now were to say, "Your head shall fall down", surely your head would fall down. (Salavatya) ‘Will you permit me, sir, to learn (this of you ?) ‘Learn’, said (Jaivali).

sa: सर्वाणि ह वा इमानि भूतान्य् आकाशाद् एव समुत्पद्यन्ते ।
iast: sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāny ākāśād eva samutpadyante ।

tr.text: (Salavatya) ‘What is the essence of this world ?’ ‘Akasa’ said (Pravahana); ‘All these beings arise from Akasa alone and are finally dissolved into Akasa; because Akasa alone is greater than all these and Akasa is the support at all times.’

sa: परोवरीयो हास्य भवति परोवरीयसो ह लोकाञ् जयति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् परोवरीयांसम् उद्गीथम् उपास्ते ॥
iast: parovarīyo hāsya bhavati parovarīyaso ha lokāñ jayati ya etad evaṃ vidvān parovarīyāṃsam udgītham upāste ॥

tr.text: It is this Udgitha which is progressively higher and better. This again is endless. He who, knowing thus, meditates upon the progressively higher and better Udgitha, obtains progressively higher and better lives and wins progressively higher and better worlds.

sa: यावत् त एनं प्रजायाम् उद्गीथं वेदिष्यन्ते परोवरीयो हैभ्यस् तावद् अस्मिंल् लोके जीवनं भविष्यति ॥
iast: yāvat ta enaṃ prajāyām udgīthaṃ vediṣyante parovarīyo haibhyas tāvad asmiṃl loke jīvanaṃ bhaviṣyati ॥

tr.text: Atidhanvan, the son of Sunaka, having taught this to Udarasandilya, said, ‘As long as among your descendants, this knowledge of the Udgitha continues, so long their life in this world will be progressively higher and better than ordinary lives.’

sa: स य एतम् एव विद्वान् उपास्ते परोवरीय एव हास्यामुष्मिंल् लोके जीवनं भवति तथामुष्मिंल् लोके लोक इति लोके लोक इति ॥
iast: sa ya etam eva vidvān upāste parovarīya eva hāsyāmuṣmiṃl loke jīvanaṃ bhavati tathāmuṣmiṃl loke loka iti loke loka iti ॥

tr.text: ‘And in that other world also their state will be similar’. He who knows and meditates thus – his life in this world surely becomes progressively higher and better, and so also his state in that other world – yea, in that other world.

sa: मटचीहतेषु कुरुष्व् आटिक्या सह जाययोषस्तिर् ह चाक्रायण इभ्यग्रामे प्रद्राणक उवास ॥
iast: maṭacīhateṣu kuruṣv āṭikyā saha jāyayoṣastir ha cākrāyaṇa ibhyagrāme pradrāṇaka uvāsa ॥

tr.text: When the crops in the Kuru country had been destroyed by hailstorms, there lived Usasti, the son of Cakra with his young wife in a deplorable condition in the village of elephant-drivers.

sa: नेतो ऽन्ये विद्यन्ते यच् च ये म इम उपनिहिता इति ॥
iast: neto ’nye vidyante yac ca ye ma ima upanihitā iti ॥

tr.text: He begged food of an elephant-driver, while he was eating beans of an inferior quality. The driver said to him, ‘There is no other food than what is set before me’.

sa: उच्छिष्टं वै मे पीतं स्याद् इति होवाच ॥
iast: ucchiṣṭaṃ vai me pītaṃ syād iti hovāca ॥

tr.text: ‘Give me some of them’, said Usasti. The driver gave them to him and said, ‘Here is drink at hand, if you please 1’ ‘Then I shall be drinking what is defiled’, said Usasti.

sa: न स्विद् एते ऽप्य् उच्छिष्टा इति ।
न वा अजीविष्यम् इमान् अखादन्न् इति होवाच ।
iast: na vā ajīviṣyam imān akhādann iti hovāca ।

tr.text: ‘Are not these beans also defiled ?’ ‘Unless I ate them, I would surely not have survived’, said Usasti, ‘but drinking is at my option’.
Usasti, after he had eaten, brought the remainder to his wife. She had already obtained her food by alms; so after receiving it she kept it by.

Next morning while leaving the bed he said, ‘Alas, if I could get a little of food, I could earn a little wealth. There a king is going to institute a sacrifice; he would appoint me to all the priestly offices’.

sa: हन्त पत इम एव कुल्माषा इति ।
iast: hanta pata ima eva kulmāṣā iti ।

tr.text: His wife said to him, ‘Well, lord, here are the beans (given by you).’ Having eaten them he went off to that sacrifice which was being performed.
Seeing the singing priests seated there, he sat down near the singers in the place for singing the Stotras. And then he addressed the Prastotir priest.

sa: प्रस्तोतर् या देवता प्रस्तावम् अन्वायत्ता तां चेद् अविद्वान् प्रस्तोष्यसि मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति ॥
iast: prastotar yā devatā prastāvam anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān prastoṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti ॥

tr.text: ‘O Prastotir, if you sing the Prastava without knowing the deity that belongs to the Prastava, your head will fall down’.

sa: उद्गातर् या देवतोद्गीथम् अन्वायत्ता तां चेद् अविद्वान् उद्गास्यसि मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति ॥
iast: udgātar yā devatodgītham anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān udgāsyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti ॥

tr.text: In the same manner he addressed the Udgatir priest, O Udgatir, if you sing the Udgitha without knowing the deity that belongs to the Udgitha, your head will fall down’.

sa: प्रतिहर्तर् या देवता प्रतिहारम् अन्वायत्ता तां चेद् अविद्वान् प्रतिहरिष्यसि मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति ।
ते ह समारतास् तूष्णीम् आसां चक्रिरे ॥
iast: pratihartar yā devatā pratihāram anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān pratihariṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti ।
te ha samāratās tūṣṇīm āsāṃ cakrire ॥

tr.text: In the same manner he addressed the Pratihartir priest, ‘O Pratihartir, if you sing the Pratihara without knowing the deity that belongs to the Pratihara, your head will fall down’. Then they all sat down silently suspending their duties.
Then the principal of the sacrifice said to him, I should like to know you, revered sir, ‘I am Chakrayana Usasti’, said he.

sa: भगवन्तं वा अहम् एभिः सर्वैर् आर्त्विज्यैः पर्यैषिषम् ।
iast: bhagavantaṃ vā aham ebhiḥ sarvair ārtvijyaiḥ paryaiṣiṣam ।

tr.text: He said, ‘I searched for you, revered sir, for all these priestly offices, but not finding you, sir, I have chosen others.’

sa: भगवांस् त्व् एव मे सर्वैर् आर्त्विज्यैर् इति ।
अथ तर्ह्य् एत एव समतिसृष्टाः स्तुवताम् ।
यावत् त्व् एभ्यो धनं दद्यास् तावन् मम दद्या इति ।
iast: bhagavāṃs tv eva me sarvair ārtvijyair iti ।
atha tarhy eta eva samatisṛṣṭāḥ stuvatām ।
yāvat tv ebhyo dhanaṃ dadyās tāvan mama dadyā iti ।

tr.text: ‘Revered sir, you yourself take up all the priestly offices for me’. ‘Be it so; then, let these same priests sing the hymns, being permitted by me. But you should give me as much wealth as you give them.’ ‘Very well’, said the sacrificer.

sa: प्रस्तोतर् या देवता प्रस्तावम् अन्वायत्ता तां चेद् अविद्वान् प्रस्तोष्यसि मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति मा भगवान् अवोचत् ।
iast: prastotar yā devatā prastāvam anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān prastoṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mā bhagavān avocat ।

tr.text: Then the Prastotir priest approached him and said, ‘Revered sir, you said to me: ‘O Prastotir, if you sing the Prastava without knowing the deity that belongs to the Prastava, your head will fall down". Which is that deity ?’

sa: सर्वाणि ह वा इमानि भूतानि प्राणम् एवाभिसंविशन्ति ।
तां चेद् अविद्वान् प्रास्तोष्यो मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यत् तथोक्तस्य मयेति ॥
iast: sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāni prāṇam evābhisaṃviśanti ।
tāṃ ced avidvān prāstoṣyo mūrdhā te vipatiṣyat tathoktasya mayeti ॥

tr.text: ‘Prana’, said Usasti, ‘all these movable and immovable beings merge in Prana (during dissolution) and rise out of Prana (during creation). This is the deity that belongs to the Prastava. If you sang the Prastava without knowing him, after your having been warned thus by me, your head would have fallen down.’

sa: उद्गातर् या देवतोद्गीथम् अन्वायत्ता तां चेद् अविद्वान् उद्गास्यसि मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति मा भगवान् अवोचत् ।
iast: udgātar yā devatodgītham anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān udgāsyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mā bhagavān avocat ।

tr.text: Then the Udgatir priest approached him and said, ‘Revered sir, you said to me: ‘O Udgatir, if you sing the Udgitha without knowing the deity that belongs to the Udgitha, your head will fall down". Which is that deity ?’

sa: सर्वाणि ह वा इमानि भूतान्य् आदित्यम् उच्चैः सन्तं गायन्ति ।
तां चेद् अविद्वान् उदगास्यो मूर्धा ते व्यपतिष्यत् तथोक्तस्य मयेति ॥
iast: sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāny ādityam uccaiḥ santaṃ gāyanti ।
tāṃ ced avidvān udagāsyo mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyat tathoktasya mayeti ॥

tr.text: ‘The sun’, said Usasti, ‘all these movable and immovable sing the praise of the sun when he has come up. This is the deity that belongs to the Udgitha. If you sang the Udgitha without knowing him, after your having been warned thus by me, your head would have fallen down.’

sa: प्रतिहर्तर् या देवता प्रतिहारम् अन्वायत्ता तां चेद् अविद्वान् प्रतिहरिष्यसि मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति मा भगवान् अवोचत् ।
iast: pratihartar yā devatā pratihāram anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān pratihariṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mā bhagavān avocat ।

tr.text: Then the Pratihartir priest approached him and said, ‘Revered sir, you said to me: ‘O Pratihartir, if you sing the Pratihara without knowing the deity that belongs to the Pratihara, your head will fall down". Which is that deity ?’

sa: सर्वाणि ह वा इमानि भूतन्य् अन्नम् एव प्रतिहरमाणानि जीवन्ति ।
तां चेद् अविद्वान् प्रत्यहरिष्यो मूर्धा ते व्यपतिष्यत् तथोक्तस्य मयेति तथोक्तस्य मयेति ॥
iast: sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtany annam eva pratiharamāṇāni jīvanti ।
tāṃ ced avidvān pratyahariṣyo mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyat tathoktasya mayeti tathoktasya mayeti ॥

tr.text: ‘Food’, said Usasti, ‘all these movable and immovable beings live by partaking of food only. This is the deity that belongs to the Pratihara. If you sang the Pratihara without knowing him, after your having been warned thus by me, your head would have fallen down.’

sa: तद् ध बको दाल्भ्यो ग्लावो वा मैत्रेयः स्वाध्यायम् उद्वव्राज ॥
iast: tad dha bako dālbhyo glāvo vā maitreyaḥ svādhyāyam udvavrāja ॥

tr.text: Therefore next begins the Udgitha seen by the dogs. Once Dalbhya Baka, called also Maitreya Glava, went out (of the village) for the study of the Vedas.
Before him a white dog appeared and other dogs gathered around it and said, ‘Revered sir, please obtain food for us by singing; we are hungry.’

sa: तद् ध बको दाल्भ्यो ग्लावो वा मैत्रेयः प्रतिपालयां चकार ॥
iast: tad dha bako dālbhyo glāvo vā maitreyaḥ pratipālayāṃ cakāra ॥

tr.text: The white dog said to them, ‘Come to me over here tomorrow morning.’ (The sage named) Dalbhya Baka and Maitreya Glava kept watch there for them.

sa: ते ह यथैवेदं बहिष्पवमानेन स्तोष्यमाणाः संरब्धाः सर्पन्तीत्य् एवम् आससृपुः ।
iast: te ha yathaivedaṃ bahiṣpavamānena stoṣyamāṇāḥ saṃrabdhāḥ sarpantīty evam āsasṛpuḥ ।

tr.text: Just as those who recite the Stotras singing the Bahispavamana hymn move along clasping one another’s hand, even so did the dogs move along. Then they sat down and began to pronounce ‘him’.

sa: ओं३ देवो वरुणः प्रजापतिः सविता२ऽन्नम् इहा२ऽहरत् ।
iast: oṃ3 devo varuṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ savitā2’nnam ihā2’harat ।

tr.text: ‘Om, let us eat ! Om, let us drink ! Om, may the (sun who is) god, Varuna, Prajapati and Savitir bring us food here. O Lord of food, bring food here, yea bring it, Om !’
Verily, this world is the syllable ‘hau’ (which is a Stobha), the air is the syllable ‘hai’, the moon is the syllable ‘atha’, the self is the syllable ‘iha’ and the fire is the syllable ‘I’.

The sun is the syllable ‘u’ (which is a Stobha), invocation is the syllable ‘e’ the Visvadevas are the syllable ‘auhoyi’, Prajapati is the syllable ‘him’, Prana is the Stobha ‘svara’, food is the Stobha ‘ya’ and Virat is the Stobha ‘vak’.

words: a chanted interjection in a Sāman (such as hum)
the sound hum (esp. expressive of menace or contempt etc.)

tr.text: The undefinable and variable thirteenth Stobha is the syllable ‘hum’.

sa: दुग्धे ऽस्मै वाग् दोहं यो वाचो दोहः ।
य एताम् एवं साम्नाम् उपनिषदं वेदोपनिषदं वेद ॥
iast: dugdhe ’smai vāg dohaṃ yo vāco dohaḥ ।
ya etām evaṃ sāmnām upaniṣadaṃ vedopaniṣadaṃ veda ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise
(according to some) the sitting down at the feet of another to listen to his wor

tr.text: For him, speech yields the milk, which is the benefit of speech; and he becomes richin food and an eater of food, who thus knows this sacred doctrine of the Samans – yea, knows the sacred doctrine of the Samans.

sa: यत् खलु साधु तत् सामेत्य् आचक्षते ।
iast: yat khalu sādhu tat sāmety ācakṣate ।
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise
the act of sitting or being near or at hand
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Om. Surely, the meditation on the whole Saman is good. Anything that is good, people call as Saman, anything that is not good, as Asaman.

sa: साम्नैनम् उपागाद् इति साधुनैनम् उपागाद् इत्य् एव तद् आहुः ।
असाम्नैनम् उपागाद् इत्य् असाधुनैनम् उपगाद् इत्य् एव तद् आहुः ॥
iast: sāmnainam upāgād iti sādhunainam upāgād ity eva tad āhuḥ ।
asāmnainam upāgād ity asādhunainam upagād ity eva tad āhuḥ ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Thus, when people say, ‘He approached him with Saman’, then they say only this: ‘He approached him with a good motive’. And when they say, ‘He approached him with Asaman’, then they say only this" ‘He approached him with an evil motive.’

sa: साम नो बतेति यत् साधु भवति साधु बतेत्य् एव तद् आहुः ।
असाम नो बतेति यद् असाधु भवत्य् असाधु बतेत्य् एव तद् आहुः ॥
iast: sāma no bateti yat sādhu bhavati sādhu batety eva tad āhuḥ ।
asāma no bateti yad asādhu bhavaty asādhu batety eva tad āhuḥ ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise
an interjection expressing astonishment or regret
an interjection expressing astonishment or regret
an interjection expressing astonishment or regret
an interjection expressing astonishment or regret

tr.text: Again, people say: ‘Oh, this is Saman for us’, when it is something good; then they say only this: ‘Oh, this is good for us’. Again, they say, ‘Oh, this is Asaman for us’, when it is not good; then they say only this: ‘Oh, this is evil.’

sa: स य एतद् एवं विद्वान् साधु सामेत्य् उपास्ते ऽभ्याशो ह यद् एनं साधवो धर्मा आ च गच्छेयुर् उप च नमेयुः ॥
iast: sa ya etad evaṃ vidvān sādhu sāmety upāste ’bhyāśo ha yad enaṃ sādhavo dharmā ā ca gaccheyur upa ca nameyuḥ ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise
that which is established or firm

tr.text: When one who knows it thus meditates on the Saman as good, all good qualities hasten towards him and serve him.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Among the worlds one should meditate upon the Saman as fivefold. The earth is the syllable him, the fire is Prasrava, the sky is Udgitha, the sun is Pratihara, and heaven is Nidhana. Thus this meditation pertains to the higher worlds.
Now, among the lower worlds. Heaven is the syllable him, the sun is Prastava, the sky is Udgitha the fire is Pratihara, and the earth is Nidhana.

sa: कल्पन्ते हास्मै लोका ऊर्ध्वाश् चावृत्तश् च य एतद् एवं विद्वांल् लोकेषु पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: kalpante hāsmai lokā ūrdhvāś cāvṛttaś ca ya etad evaṃ vidvāṃl lokeṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥
words: to be well ordered or regulated
to turn or draw round or back or near
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: The worlds in the ascending and descending lines belong to him. Who, knowing it thus (endowed with the quality of ‘good’) meditates on the fivefold Saman in the worlds.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: One should meditate on the fivefold Saman as rain. The wind that precedes is the syllable him, the cloud that is formed is Prastava, the shower is Udgitha, lightning and thunder are Pratihara, and the ceasing is Nidhana. It rains for him – indeed, he causes rain – who, knowing it thus, meditates on the fivefold Saman as rain.

sa: उद्गृह्णाति तन् निधनं वर्षयति ह य एतद् एवं विद्वान् वृष्टौ पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: udgṛhṇāti tan nidhanaṃ varṣayati ha ya etad evaṃ vidvān vṛṣṭau pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥
words: to cause to rain (Parjanya etc.) or to fall down as rain (flowers etc.)
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: One should meditate on the fivefold Saman as rain. The wind that precedes is the syllable him, the cloud that is formed is Prastava, the shower is Udgitha, lightning and thunder are Pratihara, and the ceasing is Nidhana. It rains for him – indeed, he causes rain – who, knowing it thus, meditates on the fivefold Saman as rain.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise
a tiger (as making a lowing or roaring sound)
chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions

tr.text: One should meditate on the fivefold Saman in all the waters. When a cloud gathers, it is the syllable him. When it rains, it is Prastava. Those (waters) that flow to the east, are Udgitha. Those that flow to the west are Pratihara. The ocean is Nidhana.

sa: न हाप्सु प्रैत्य् अप्सुमान् भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् सर्वास्व् अप्सु पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: na hāpsu praity apsumān bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān sarvāsv apsu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥
words: possessed of or shining in the waters (e.g. the lightning which does not lose it
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: He who, knowing it thus, meditates on the fivefold Saman in all the waters, does not drown in water and he becomes rich in water.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: One should meditate on the fivefold Saman as the seasons: The spring is the syllable him, the summer is Prastava, the rainy season is Udgitha, the autumn is Pratihara, and the winter is Nidhana.

sa: कल्पन्ते हास्मा ऋतव ऋतुमान् भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् ऋतुषु पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: kalpante hāsmā ṛtava ṛtumān bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān ṛtuṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥
words: to be well ordered or regulated
coming at regular or proper times
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: He, who knowing it thus, meditates on the fivefold Saman in the seasons, him the seasons serve and he becomes rich in seasons.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: One should meditate on the fivefold Saman as the animals. The goats are the syllable him, the sheep are Prastava, the cows are Udgitha, the horses are Pratihara, and man is Nidhana.

sa: भवन्ति हास्य पशवः पशुमान् भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् पशुषु पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: bhavanti hāsya paśavaḥ paśumān bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān paśuṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥
words: connected with or relating to cattle or animals
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: He, who knowing it this, meditates on the fivefold Saman in animals, to him animals belong and he becomes rich in animals.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: One should meditate on the progressively higher and better fivefold Saman as the senses; The organ of smell is the syllable him, the organ of speech is Prastava, the eye is Udgitha, the ear is Pratihara, and the mind is Nidhana. Verily, these are progressively higher and better.

sa: परोवरीयो हास्य भवति परोवरीयसो ह लोकाञ् जयति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् प्राणेषु पञ्चविधं परोवरीयः सामोपास्ते ।
iast: parovarīyo hāsya bhavati parovarīyaso ha lokāñ jayati ya etad evaṃ vidvān prāṇeṣu pañcavidhaṃ parovarīyaḥ sāmopāste ।
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: He who knowing it thus, meditates on the fivefold Saman, progressively higher and better, in the senses, to him belong progressively higher and better lives and he wins ever higher and better worlds. So much for (the meditation on) the fivefold Saman.

sa: यत् किंच वाचो हुम् इति स हिङ्कारः ।
iast: yat kiṃca vāco hum iti sa hiṅkāraḥ ।
words: a tiger (as making a lowing or roaring sound)

tr.text: Next is the meditation on the sevenfold Saman. One should meditate on the sevenfold Saman as speech. Whatsoever in speech is ‘hum’, that is the syllable him; whatever is ‘pra’, that is Prastava; whatever is ‘a’, that is Adi (the first); whatever is ‘ut’, that is Udgitha; whatever is ‘prati’, that is Pratihara; whetever is ‘upa’, that is Upadrava; and whatever is ‘ni’, that is Nidhana.

Next is the meditation on the sevenfold Saman. One should meditate on the sevenfold Saman as speech. Whatsoever in speech is ‘hum’, that is the syllable him; whatever is ‘pra’, that is Prastava; whatever is ‘a’, that is Adi (the first); whatever is ‘ut’, that is Udgitha; whatever is ‘prati’, that is Pratihara; whetever is ‘upa’, that is Upadrava; and whatever is ‘ni’, that is Nidhana.

sa: दुग्धे ऽस्मै वाग् दोहं यो वाचो दोहः ।
य एतद् एवं विद्वान् वाचि सप्तविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: dugdhe ’smai vāg dohaṃ yo vāco dohaḥ ।
ya etad evaṃ vidvān vāci saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: He who knowing it thus, meditates on the sevenfold (whole) Saman as speech, for him speech yields milk i.e. its appropriate benefit, and he becomes rich in food and an eater of food.

sa: अथ खल्व् अमुम् आदित्यं सप्तविधं सामोपासीत ।
मां प्रति मां प्रतीति सर्वेण समस् तेन साम ॥
iast: atha khalv amum ādityaṃ saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta ।
māṃ prati māṃ pratīti sarveṇa samas tena sāma ॥

tr.text: Next, one should meditate upon the sevenfold Saman as the yonder sun. He is the Saman because he is always the same. He is the Saman because he is the same to all, for each one thinks, ‘He faces me, he faces me.’

sa: तस्मिन्न् इमानि सर्वाणि भूतान्य् अन्वायत्तानीति विद्यात् ।
iast: tasminn imāni sarvāṇi bhūtāny anvāyattānīti vidyāt ।

tr.text: One should know that all these beings are dependent on him. What he is before rising, that is Himkara. On this, the animals are dependent. As they participate in the Himkara part of this Saman, do they utter him (before sunrise).

Then, the form of the sun when it has just risen, that is Prastava. On this, men are dependent. As they participate in the Prastava part of this Saman, so are they desirous of praise, direct and indirect.

sa: तस्मात् तान्य् अन्तरिक्षे ऽनारम्भणान्य् आदायात्मानं परिपतन्ति ।

tr.text: And the form of the sun as it appears at the time of the assembling of its rays, that is Adi. On this, the birds are dependent. As they participate in the Adi part of this Saman, so do they hold themselves unsupported in the sky and fly about.

sa: अथ यत् संप्रति मध्यंदिने स उद्गीथः ।
iast: atha yat saṃprati madhyaṃdine sa udgīthaḥ ।

tr.text: Next, the form of the sun that appears just at midday, that is Udgitha. On this, the gods are dependent. As they participate in the Udgitha part of this Saman, so are they the best among the offsprings of Prajapati.

sa: अथ यद् ऊर्ध्वं मध्यंदिनात् प्राग् अपराह्णात् स प्रतिहारः ।
iast: atha yad ūrdhvaṃ madhyaṃdināt prāg aparāhṇāt sa pratihāraḥ ।

tr.text: Next, the form of the sun that appears just after midday and before (the latter part of) afternoon, that is Pratihara. On this, the foetuses are dependent. As they participate in the Pratihara part of this Saman, (so are they held up in the womb) and they do not fall down.

sa: अथ यद् ऊर्ध्वम् अपराह्णात् प्राग् अस्तम् अयात् स उपद्रवः ।
तस्मात् ते पुरुषं दृष्ट्वा कक्षं श्वभ्रम् इत्य् उपद्रवन्ति ।
iast: atha yad ūrdhvam aparāhṇāt prāg astam ayāt sa upadravaḥ ।
tasmāt te puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā kakṣaṃ śvabhram ity upadravanti ।

tr.text: Next, the form of the sun that appears when it is past afternoon and before sunset, that is Upadrava. On this, the wild animals are dependent. As they participate in the Upadrava part of this Saman, so do they, when they see a man, run away to the forest, as to a place of safety.

sa: एवं खल्व् अमुम् आदित्यं सप्तविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: evaṃ khalv amum ādityaṃ saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥

tr.text: Now, the form of the sun that appears just after sunset, that is Nidhana. On this, the fathers are dependent. As they participate in the Nidhana part of this Saman, so do people lay them aside.

sa: अथ खल्व् आत्मसंमितम् अतिमृत्यु सप्तविधं सामोपासीत ।
iast: atha khalv ātmasaṃmitam atimṛtyu saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta ।
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Now, verily, one should meditate on the sevenfold Saman, which has all its parts similar, and which leads beyond death. ‘Himkara, has three syllables; ‘Prastava’ has three syllables. So they are equal to each other.
‘Adi’ has two syllables; ‘Pratihara’ has four syllables. We take one syllable from Pratihara to Adi. So they are equal to each other.

sa: उद्गीथ इति त्र्यक्षरम् उपद्रव इति चतुरक्षरं त्रिभिस् त्रिभिः समं भवति ।
iast: udgītha iti tryakṣaram upadrava iti caturakṣaraṃ tribhis tribhiḥ samaṃ bhavati ।
words: chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions
that which attacks or occurs suddenly

tr.text: ‘Udgitha’ has three syllables; ‘Upadrava’ has four syllables. Three and three become equal. One syllable is left over; that really is tri-syllabic; so it also becomes equal.

sa: तानि ह वा एतानि द्वाविंशतिर् अक्षराणि ॥
iast: tāni ha vā etāni dvāviṃśatir akṣarāṇi ॥

tr.text: ‘Nidhana’ has three syllables, and this to is equal (to the others). These, indeed, are the twenty two syllables (of the sevenfold Saman).

words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere

tr.text: He who, knowing this Saman thus (as good), meditates on the sevenfold Saman, which has all its parts similar and which leads beyond death, reaches the sun (Death) by the number twenty-one; for, counting from this world the yonder sun is verily the twenty-first. With the remaining twenty-second syllable he conquers the world beyond the sun. That world is of the nature of bliss, and is free from misery. (That is), he obtains victory over the sun, and then a victory still higher becomes his, who meditates on the sevenfold Saman.

sa: परो हास्यादित्यजयाज् जयो भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् आत्मसंमितम् अतिमृत्यु सप्तविधं सामोपास्ते सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: paro hāsyādityajayāj jayo bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān ātmasaṃmitam atimṛtyu saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste sāmopāste ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
a metrical hymn or song of praise
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: He who, knowing this Saman thus (as good), meditates on the sevenfold Saman, which has all its parts similar and which leads beyond death, reaches the sun (Death) by the number twenty-one; for, counting from this world the yonder sun is verily the twenty-first. With the remaining twenty-second syllable he conquers the world beyond the sun. That world is of the nature of bliss, and is free from misery. (That is), he obtains victory over the sun, and then a victory still higher becomes his, who meditates on the sevenfold Saman.

words: a hymn composed in the Gāyatrī metre

tr.text: The mind is Himkara, speech is Prastava, the eye is Udgitha, the ear is Pratihara, and the Prana is Nidhana. This is the Gayatra Saman woven in (the Prana and) the senses.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् गायत्रं प्राणेषु प्रोतं वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etad gāyatraṃ prāṇeṣu protaṃ veda ।
words: a hymn composed in the Gāyatrī metre

tr.text: He who thus knows this Gayatra Saman as woven in (the Prana and) the senses, becomes the possessor of perfect senses, reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should be high-minded.

One rubs, that is Himkara. The smoke is produced, that is Prastava. It blazes, that is Udgitha. The embers are formed, that is Pratihara. It goes down, that is Nidhana. It is completely extinguished, that is Nidhana. This is the Rathantara Saman woven in fire.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् रथंतरम् अग्नौ प्रोतं वेद ।
न प्रत्यङ्ङ् अग्निम् आचामेन् न निष्ठीवेत् ।
iast: sa ya evam etad rathaṃtaram agnau protaṃ veda ।
na pratyaṅṅ agnim ācāmen na niṣṭhīvet ।
words: to sip (water) from the palm of the hand for purification

tr.text: He who thus knows this Rathantara Saman as woven in fire becomes radiant with the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom, is endowed with good appetite and reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should neither sip nor spit facing the fire.

sa: प्रति स्त्रीं सह शेते स प्रतिहारः ।
iast: prati strīṃ saha śete sa pratihāraḥ ।

tr.text: The Vamadevya Saman is woven in a couple. He who thus knows this Vamadevya Saman as woven in a couple becomes one of the couple and procreates. He reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not despise any woman.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् वामदेव्यं मिथुने प्रोतं वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etad vāmadevyaṃ mithune protaṃ veda ।

tr.text: The Vamadevya Saman is woven in a couple. He who thus knows this Vamadevya Saman as woven in a couple becomes one of the couple and procreates. He reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not despise any woman.
The rising sun is Himkara; the risen sun is Prastava; the midday sun is Udgitha; the sun in the afternoon is Pratihara, and the setting sun is Nidhana. This is the Brihat Saman woven in the sun.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् बृहद् आदित्ये प्रोतं वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etad bṛhad āditye protaṃ veda ।

tr.text: He who thus knows this Brihat Saman as woven in the sun becomes refulgent and endowed with good appetite, reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not find fault with the burning sun.

words: a tiger (as making a lowing or roaring sound)

tr.text: The white clouds gather, that is Himkara. The (rain-bearing) cloud is formed, that is Prastava. It rains, that is Udgitha. It flashes and thunders, that is Pratihara. It ceases, that is Nidhana. This is the Vairupa Saman woven in the rain-cloud.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् वैरूपं पर्जन्ये प्रोतं वेद ।
विरूपांश् च सुरूपंश् च पशून् अवरुन्धे ।
iast: sa ya evam etad vairūpaṃ parjanye protaṃ veda ।
virūpāṃś ca surūpaṃś ca paśūn avarundhe ।

tr.text: He who thus knows this Virupa Saman as woven in the rain-cloud acquires cattle of handsome and manifold forms, reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not find fault with the rain-cloud when it rains.
The spring is Himkara, the summer is Prastava, the rainy season is Udgitha, the autumn is Pratihara, and the winter is Nidhana. This is the Vairaja Saman woven in the seasons.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् वैराजम् ऋतुषु प्रोतं वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etad vairājam ṛtuṣu protaṃ veda ।

tr.text: He who thus knows this Vairaja Saman as woven in the seasons shines with offspring, cattle and the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom, reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not find fault with the seasons.
The earth is Himkara, the sky is Prastava, heaven is Udgitha, the quarters are Pratihara, and the ocean is Nidhana. This is the Sakvari Saman woven in the worlds.

sa: स य एवम् एताः शक्वर्यो लोकेषु प्रोता वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etāḥ śakvaryo lokeṣu protā veda ।

tr.text: He who thus knows this Sakvari Saman woven in the worlds, becomes the possessor of the worlds, reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not find fault with the worlds.
The goats are Himkara, the sheep are Prastava, the cows are Udgitha, the horses are Pratihara, and man is Nidhana. This is the Revati Saman woven in the animals.

sa: स य एवम् एता रेवत्यः पशुषु प्रोता वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etā revatyaḥ paśuṣu protā veda ।

tr.text: He who thus knows this Revati Saman woven in the animals, becomes the possessor of animals, reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not find fault with animals.

words: Name des letzten stotra bei der Abendpressung im agniṣṭoma

tr.text: The hair is Himkara, the skin is Prastava, the flesh is Udgitha, the bone is Pratihara, and the marrow is Nidhana. This is the Yajnayajniya Saman woven in the limbs of the body.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् यज्ञायज्ञीयम् अङ्गेषु प्रोतं वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etad yajñāyajñīyam aṅgeṣu protaṃ veda ।
words: Name des letzten stotra bei der Abendpressung im agniṣṭoma

tr.text: He who thus knows this Yajnayajniya Saman, woven in the limbs of the body, is endowed with all the limbs, and is not crippled in any limb; he reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not eat fish and meat for a year, or rather, he should not eat fish and meat at all.
Fire is Himkara, Air is Prastava, the Sun is Udgitha, the Stars are Pratihara, and the Moon is Nidhana. This is the Rajana Saman woven in the deities.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् राजनं देवतासु प्रोतं वेद ।
एतासाम् एव देवतानां सलोकतां सर्ष्टितां सायुज्यं गच्छति ।
iast: sa ya evam etad rājanaṃ devatāsu protaṃ veda ।
etāsām eva devatānāṃ salokatāṃ sarṣṭitāṃ sāyujyaṃ gacchati ।
words: the being in the same world or sphere with

tr.text: He who knows thus knows this Rajana Saman woven in the deities, abides in the same world or gets the same prosperity as these very deities or attains union with them; he reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not find fault with the Brahmanas.

words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions
a star or any heavenly body

tr.text: The three Vedas are Himkara; the three worlds are Prastava; Fire, Air and the Sun are Udgitha; the Stars, the birds and the rays are Pratihara; the serpents, the celestial singers and the fathers are Nidhana. This is the collection of Samans woven in all things.

sa: स य एवम् एतत् साम सर्वस्मिन् प्रोतं वेद सर्वं ह भवति ॥
iast: sa ya evam etat sāma sarvasmin protaṃ veda sarvaṃ ha bhavati ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Verily, he who thus knows this collection of Samans as woven in all things becomes the lord of all things.

sa: तेभ्यो न ज्यायः परम् अन्यद् अस्ति ॥
iast: tebhyo na jyāyaḥ param anyad asti ॥

tr.text: There is this verse about it: That which is fivefold in groups of three – there is nothing else greater or other than these (fifteen).

sa: यस् तद् वेद स वेद सर्वम् ।
iast: yas tad veda sa veda sarvam ।

tr.text: He who knows that knows all. All the quarters bring offerings to him. His holy vow is that he should meditate ‘I am all’ – yea, that is his vow.

sa: विनर्दि साम्नो वृणे पशव्यम् इत्य् अग्नेर् उद्गीथः ।
iast: vinardi sāmno vṛṇe paśavyam ity agner udgīthaḥ ।

tr.text: ‘Of the Samans, I choose the one that bellows, as it were, and is good for cattle,’ thus (some think). This is the loud singing sacred to Agni, the undefined one to Prajapati, the defined one to Soma, the soft and smooth to Vayu, the smooth and strong to Indra, the heron-like to Brihaspati, and the illsounding to Varuna. Verily, one may practise all these, but should avoid the one sacred to Varuna.

sa: स्वधां पितृभ्य आशां मनुष्येभ्यस् तृणोदकं पशुभ्यः स्वर्गं लोकं यजमानायान्नम् आत्मन आगायानीत्य् एतानि मनसा ध्यायन्न् अप्रमत्तः स्तुवीत ॥
iast: svadhāṃ pitṛbhya āśāṃ manuṣyebhyas tṛṇodakaṃ paśubhyaḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ yajamānāyānnam ātmana āgāyānīty etāni manasā dhyāyann apramattaḥ stuvīta ॥

tr.text: ‘May I obtain immortality for the gods by singing’, (thinking) thus one should sing. ‘May I obtain my singing, oblation for the fathers, hope for men, grass and water for animals, the heavenly world for the sacrificer, and food for myself’, -- thus reflecting in his mind on all these, he should sing the Stotra attentively.

sa: इन्द्रं शरणं प्रपन्नो ऽभूवं स त्वा प्रति वक्ष्यतीत्य् एनं ब्रूयात् ॥
iast: indraṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanno ’bhūvaṃ sa tvā prati vakṣyatīty enaṃ brūyāt ॥

tr.text: All vowels are the embodiments of Indra; all sibilants are the embodiments of Prajapati; all Sparsa consonants are the embodiments of Death. If anyone should reprove him for the pronunciation of his vowels, he should tell him, ‘I have taken my refuge in Indra; he will answer you.’

sa: प्रजापतिं शरणं प्रपन्नो ऽभूवं स त्वा प्रति पेक्ष्यतीत्य् एनं ब्रूयात् ।
मृत्युं शरणं प्रपन्नो ऽभूवं स त्वा प्रति धक्ष्यतीत्य् एनं ब्रूयात् ॥
iast: prajāpatiṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanno ’bhūvaṃ sa tvā prati pekṣyatīty enaṃ brūyāt ।
mṛtyuṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanno ’bhūvaṃ sa tvā prati dhakṣyatīty enaṃ brūyāt ॥

tr.text: And if some one should reprove him for sibilants he should tell him, ‘I have taken my refuge in Prajapati; he will crush you’. And if some one should reprove him for his Sparsa consonants, he should tell him, ‘I have taken my refuge in Death; he will burn you up.’

sa: सर्वे स्वरा घोषवन्तो बलवन्तो वक्तव्या इन्द्रे बलं ददानीति ।
सर्व ऊष्माणो ऽग्रस्ता अनिरस्ता विवृता वक्तव्याः प्रजापतेर् आत्मानं परिददानीति ।
सर्वे स्पर्शा लेशेनानभिनिहिता वक्तव्या मृत्योर् आत्मानं परिहराणीति ॥
iast: sarve svarā ghoṣavanto balavanto vaktavyā indre balaṃ dadānīti ।
sarva ūṣmāṇo ’grastā anirastā vivṛtā vaktavyāḥ prajāpater ātmānaṃ paridadānīti ।
sarve sparśā leśenānabhinihitā vaktavyā mṛtyor ātmānaṃ pariharāṇīti ॥

tr.text: All vowels should be pronounced sonant and strong, (with the thought), ‘May I impart strength to Indra (Prana)’. All sibilants should be pronounced, neither inarticulately, nor leaving out the elements of sound, but distinctly (with the thought), ‘May I give myself to Prajapati (Virat).’ All Sparsa consonants should be pronounced slowly, without mixing them with any other letter, (with the thought), ‘May I withdraw myself from Death.’

sa: ब्रह्मचार्याचार्यकुलवासी तृतीयो ऽत्यन्तम् आत्मानम् आचार्यकुले ऽवसादयन् ।

tr.text: Three are the branches of religious duty. Sacrifice, study and gifts – these are the first. Austerity alone is the second, and the celibate student of sacred knowledge, who lives in the house of the teacher throughout his life mortifying his body in the teacher’s house, is the third. All these become possessors of meritorious worlds; but he who is established firmly in Brahman, attains immortality.

sa: तस्या अभितप्ताया एतान्य् अक्षराणि संप्रस्र्वन्त भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति ॥
iast: tasyā abhitaptāyā etāny akṣarāṇi saṃprasrvanta bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti ॥

tr.text: Prajapati brooded on the worlds. From them, thus brooded upon, issued forth the threefold Veda (as their essence). He brooded on this. From this, thus brooded upon, issued forth the syllables Bhuh, Bhuvah and Svah.

sa: तद् यथा शङ्कुना सर्वाणि पर्णानि संतृण्णान्य् एवम् ओंकारेण सर्वा वाक् संतृण्णा ।
ओंकार एवेदं सर्वम् ओंकार एव इदं सर्वम् ॥
iast: tad yathā śaṅkunā sarvāṇi parṇāni saṃtṛṇṇāny evam oṃkāreṇa sarvā vāk saṃtṛṇṇā ।
oṃkāra evedaṃ sarvam oṃkāra eva idaṃ sarvam ॥

tr.text: He brooded on them. From them, thus brooded upon, issued forth (as their essence) the syllable Om (Brahman). Just as all the parts of the leaf, are permeated by the ribs of the leaf, so are all the words permeated by the syllable Om. Verily, the syllable Om is all this – yea, the syllable Om is verily all this.

sa: आदित्यानां च विश्वेषां च देवानां तृतीयसवनम् ॥
iast: ādityānāṃ ca viśveṣāṃ ca devānāṃ tṛtīyasavanam ॥

tr.text: The expounders of Brahman say, ‘The morning libation is of the Vasus, the midday libation is of the Rudras and the third libation is of the Adityas and of the Visvadevas. Where, the, is the world of the sacrificer ?’ How can he who does not know this, perform (sacrifices) ? It is only after knowing this that he should perform (sacrifices).

sa: स यस् तं न विद्यात् कथं कुर्यात् ।
iast: sa yas taṃ na vidyāt kathaṃ kuryāt ।

tr.text: The expounders of Brahman say, ‘The morning libation is of the Vasus, the midday libation is of the Rudras and the third libation is of the Adityas and of the Visvadevas. Where, the, is the world of the sacrificer ?’ How can he who does not know this, perform (sacrifices) ? It is only after knowing this that he should perform (sacrifices).

sa: पुरा प्रातरनुवाकस्योपाकरणाज् जघनेन गार्हपत्यस्योदाङ्मुख उपविश्य स वासवं सामाभिगायति ॥
iast: purā prātaranuvākasyopākaraṇāj jaghanena gārhapatyasyodāṅmukha upaviśya sa vāsavaṃ sāmābhigāyati ॥

tr.text: Before the commencement of the morning chant, the sacrificer sits down behind the Garhapatya fire, facing the north and sings the Saman sacred to the Vasus: ‘(O Fire), open the door of this world that we may see you for obtaining the kingdom.’

iast: paśyema tvā vayaṃ rā 33333 hu 3 m ā 33 jyā 3 yo 3 ā 32111 iti ॥

tr.text: Before the commencement of the morning chant, the sacrificer sits down behind the Garhapatya fire, facing the north and sings the Saman sacred to the Vasus: ‘(O Fire), open the door of this world that we may see you for obtaining the kingdom.’

Then he offers the oblation (with the Mantra) – ‘Salutation to Fire, who dwells in the region of the earth. Obtain the region, for me the sacrificer. This region, indeed, is to be obtained by the sacrificer. At the end of the duration of this life, I, the sacrificer, am willing to come here – Svaha.’ ‘Unbar the door of the region’, saying this he gets up. (As a result) the Vasus grant him (the region connected with) the morning libation.

Then he offers the oblation (with the Mantra) – ‘Salutation to Fire, who dwells in the region of the earth. Obtain the region, for me the sacrificer. This region, indeed, is to be obtained by the sacrificer. At the end of the duration of this life, I, the sacrificer, am willing to come here – Svaha.’ ‘Unbar the door of the region’, saying this he gets up. (As a result) the Vasus grant him (the region connected with) the morning libation.

sa: पुरा माध्यन्दिनस्य सवनस्योपाकरणाज् जघनेनाग्नीध्रीयस्योदङ्मुख उपविश्य स रौद्रं सामाभिगायति ॥
iast: purā mādhyandinasya savanasyopākaraṇāj jaghanenāgnīdhrīyasyodaṅmukha upaviśya sa raudraṃ sāmābhigāyati ॥

tr.text: Before the starting of the midday libation, the sacrificer sits down behind the Agnidhriya fire, facing the north, and sings the Saman sacred to the Rudras: ‘(O Fire), open the door of the region of the sky that we may see you for obtaining the sovereignty of the sky.’

iast: paśyema tvā vayaṃ vairā 33333 hu 3 m ā 33 jyā 3 yo 3 ā 32111 iti ॥

tr.text: Before the starting of the midday libation, the sacrificer sits down behind the Agnidhriya fire, facing the north, and sings the Saman sacred to the Rudras: ‘(O Fire), open the door of the region of the sky that we may see you for obtaining the sovereignty of the sky.’

Then he offers the oblation (with the Mantra): ‘Salutation to Vayu, who dwells in the region of the sky. Obtain this region for me, the sacrificer. This region, indeed, is to be obtained by the sacrificer. At the end of the duration of this life, I, the sacrificer, am willing to go there – Svaha’. ‘Unbar the door of the region’, saying this he gets up. (As a result) the Rudras grant him (the region of the sky connected with) the midday libation.

Then he offers the oblation (with the Mantra): ‘Salutation to Vayu, who dwells in the region of the sky. Obtain this region for me, the sacrificer. This region, indeed, is to be obtained by the sacrificer. At the end of the duration of this life, I, the sacrificer, am willing to go there – Svaha’. ‘Unbar the door of the region’, saying this he gets up. (As a result) the Rudras grant him (the region of the sky connected with) the midday libation.

sa: पुरा तृतीयसवनस्योपाकरणाज् जघनेनाहवनीयस्योदङ्मुख उपविश्य स आदित्यं स वैश्वदेवं सामाभिगायति ॥
iast: purā tṛtīyasavanasyopākaraṇāj jaghanenāhavanīyasyodaṅmukha upaviśya sa ādityaṃ sa vaiśvadevaṃ sāmābhigāyati ॥

tr.text: Before beginning the third libation, the sacrificer sits down behind the Ahavaniya fire, facing the north, and sings the Saman sacred to the Adityas and the one sacred to the Visvadevas: ‘(O Fire), open the door of the region of heaven that we may see you for obtaining the sovereignty of heaven’. This is the Saman sacred to the Adityas. Next is the one sacred to the Visvadevas; ‘(O Fire), open the door of the region of heaven that we may see you for obtaining the supreme sovereignty.’

Before beginning the third libation, the sacrificer sits down behind the Ahavaniya fire, facing the north, and sings the Saman sacred to the Adityas and the one sacred to the Visvadevas: ‘(O Fire), open the door of the region of heaven that we may see you for obtaining the sovereignty of heaven’. This is the Saman sacred to the Adityas. Next is the one sacred to the Visvadevas; ‘(O Fire), open the door of the region of heaven that we may see you for obtaining the supreme sovereignty.’

sa: पश्येम त्वा वयं साम्रा ३३३३३ हु३म् आ ३३ ज्या ३ यो ३ आ ३२१११ इति ॥

tr.text: Before beginning the third libation, the sacrificer sits down behind the Ahavaniya fire, facing the north, and sings the Saman sacred to the Adityas and the one sacred to the Visvadevas: ‘(O Fire), open the door of the region of heaven that we may see you for obtaining the sovereignty of heaven’. This is the Saman sacred to the Adityas. Next is the one sacred to the Visvadevas; ‘(O Fire), open the door of the region of heaven that we may see you for obtaining the supreme sovereignty.’

sa: नम आदित्येभ्यश् च विश्वेभ्यश् च देवेभ्यो दिविक्षिद्भ्यो लोकक्षिद्भ्यः ।
iast: nama ādityebhyaś ca viśvebhyaś ca devebhyo divikṣidbhyo lokakṣidbhyaḥ ।

tr.text: Then the sacrificer offers the oblation (with the Mantra): ‘Salutation to the Adityas and to the Visvadevas, the inhabitants of the region of heaven. Obtain the region of heaven for me, the sacrificer. This region, indeed, is to be obtained by the sacrificer. At the end of the duration of this life, I, the sacrificer, am willing to go there – Svaha’. ‘Unbar the door of the region’, saying this, he gets up.

sa: एतास्म्य् अत्र यजमानः परस्ताद् आयुषः स्वाहा ।
iast: etāsmy atra yajamānaḥ parastād āyuṣaḥ svāhā ।

tr.text: Then the sacrificer offers the oblation (with the Mantra): ‘Salutation to the Adityas and to the Visvadevas, the inhabitants of the region of heaven. Obtain the region of heaven for me, the sacrificer. This region, indeed, is to be obtained by the sacrificer. At the end of the duration of this life, I, the sacrificer, am willing to go there – Svaha’. ‘Unbar the door of the region’, saying this, he gets up.

sa: तस्मा आदित्याश् च विश्वे च देवास् तृतीयसवनं संप्रयच्छन्ति ।
एष ह वै यज्ञस्य मात्रां वेद य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ॥
iast: tasmā ādityāś ca viśve ca devās tṛtīyasavanaṃ saṃprayacchanti ।
eṣa ha vai yajñasya mātrāṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: The Adityas and the Visvadevas grant him (the region appropriate to) the third libation. He alone knows the real character of the sacrifice, who knows thus.
Om. The yonder sun indeed is the honey of the gods. Of this honey, heaven is the cross-beam, the sky is the honey comb, and (the water particles in) the rays are the eggs.

sa: तस्य ये प्राञ्चो रश्मयस् ता एवास्य प्राच्यो मधुनाड्यः ।
iast: tasya ye prāñco raśmayas tā evāsya prācyo madhunāḍyaḥ ।

tr.text: The eastern rays of that sun are its eastern honey-cells; the Riks are the bees, (the ritual of) the Rig-Veda is the flower and those waters are the nectar. Those very Riks (the bees) pressed this RigVeda. From it, thus pressed, issued forth as juice, fame, splendour (of limbs), (alertness of) the senses, virility, and food for eating.

sa: तस्याभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियं वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
iast: tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso ’jāyata ॥

tr.text: The eastern rays of that sun are its eastern honey-cells; the Riks are the bees, (the ritual of) the Rig-Veda is the flower and those waters are the nectar. Those very Riks (the bees) pressed this RigVeda. From it, thus pressed, issued forth as juice, fame, splendour (of limbs), (alertness of) the senses, virility, and food for eating.

sa: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य रोहितं रूपम् ॥
iast: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya rohitaṃ rūpam ॥

tr.text: That juice flowed forth; it settled by the side of the sun. Verily, this it is that appears as the red hue of the sun.

sa: अथ ये ऽस्य दक्षिणा रश्मयस् ता एवास्य दक्षिणा मधुनाड्यः ।
iast: atha ye ’sya dakṣiṇā raśmayas tā evāsya dakṣiṇā madhunāḍyaḥ ।

tr.text: And its southern rays are its southern honey cells. The Yajus verses are the bees. The YajurVeda is the flower; and those waters are the nectar.

sa: तानि वा एतानि यजूंष्य् एतं यजुर्वेदम् अभ्यतपन् ।
तस्य अभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियं वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
iast: tāni vā etāni yajūṃṣy etaṃ yajurvedam abhyatapan ।
tasya abhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso ’jāyata ॥

tr.text: Those very Yajus verses pressed this Yajur-Veda. And from it, thus pressed, issued forth as juice, fame, splendour of limbs, alertness of the senses, virility, and food for eating.

sa: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य शुक्लं रूपम् ॥
iast: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya śuklaṃ rūpam ॥

tr.text: It, flowed forth; it settled by the side of the sun. Verily, this it is that appears as the white hue of the sun.

sa: अथ ये ऽस्य प्रत्यञ्चो रश्मायस् ता एवास्य प्रतीच्यो मधुनाड्यः ।
iast: atha ye ’sya pratyañco raśmāyas tā evāsya pratīcyo madhunāḍyaḥ ।

tr.text: And its western rays are its western honey cells. The Samans are the bees. The Sama-Veda is the flower; and those waters are the nectar.

sa: तानि वा एतानि सामान्य् एतं सामवेदम् अभ्यतपन् ।
तस्याभितप्तस्य यशस् तेज इन्द्रियं वीर्यम् अन्नाद्यं रसो ऽजायत ॥
iast: tāni vā etāni sāmāny etaṃ sāmavedam abhyatapan ।
tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso ’jāyata ॥

the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
the sap or juice of plants

tr.text: Those very Samans pressed this Sama-Veda. From it, thus pressed, issued forth as juice, fame, splendour of limbs, alertness of the senses, virility, and food for eating.

sa: तद् वा एतद् यद् एतद् आदित्यस्य कृष्णं रूपम् ॥
iast: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya kṛṣṇaṃ rūpam ॥

sa: अथ ये ऽस्योदञ्चो रश्मयस् ता एवास्योदीच्यो मधुनाड्यः ।
iast: atha ye ’syodañco raśmayas tā evāsyodīcyo madhunāḍyaḥ ।
