tr.text: And if the sacrifice is rendered defective on account of the Samans, then with the Mantra ‘Svah Svaha’ (the Brahman priest) should offer an oblation to the Ahavaniya fire. Thus verily, through the essence of the Samans, through the virility of the Saman, he makes good the injury of the sacrifice in respect of the Samans.

sa: सुवर्णेन रजतं रजतेन त्रपु त्रपुणा सीसं सीसेन लोहं लोहेन दारु दारु चर्मणा ॥
iast: suvarṇena rajataṃ rajatena trapu trapuṇā sīsaṃ sīsena lohaṃ lohena dāru dāru carmaṇā ॥
words: to place or hold or put or draw or join or fasten or fix or sew together

tr.text: Just as one would join gold with salt, silver with gold, tin with silver, lead with tin, iron with lead, wood with iron, and wood with leather, even so does (the Brahman priest) make good the injury of the sacrifice through the virility of these regions, of these deities, and of the three Vedas. That sacrifice indeed is healed where there is a Brahman priest knowing thus.

sa: एवम् एषां लोकानाम् आसां देवतानाम् अस्यास् त्रय्या विद्याया वीर्येण यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं संदधाति ।
भेषजकृतो ह वा एष यज्ञो यत्रैवंविद् ब्रह्मा भवति ॥
iast: evam eṣāṃ lokānām āsāṃ devatānām asyās trayyā vidyāyā vīryeṇa yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti ।
bheṣajakṛto ha vā eṣa yajño yatraivaṃvid brahmā bhavati ॥
words: to place or hold or put or draw or join or fasten or fix or sew together

tr.text: Just as one would join gold with salt, silver with gold, tin with silver, lead with tin, iron with lead, wood with iron, and wood with leather, even so does (the Brahman priest) make good the injury of the sacrifice through the virility of these regions, of these deities, and of the three Vedas. That sacrifice indeed is healed where there is a Brahman priest knowing thus.

sa: एष ह वा उदक्प्रवणो यज्ञो यत्रैवंविद् ब्रह्मा भवति ।
एवंविदं ह वा एषा ब्रह्माणम् अनु गाथा ।
यतो यत आवर्तते तत् तद् गच्छति ॥
iast: eṣa ha vā udakpravaṇo yajño yatraivaṃvid brahmā bhavati ।
evaṃvidaṃ ha vā eṣā brahmāṇam anu gāthā ।
yato yata āvartate tat tad gacchati ॥
words: to turn or draw round or back or near

tr.text: That sacrifice indeed becomes inclined to the north, where there is a Brahman priest knowing thus. It is in reference to the Brahman priest knowing thus that there is this song: ‘Whence-soever the sacrifice comes back, thither verily does the Brahman priest go (to remedy)’.

sa: एवंविद् ध वै ब्रह्मा यज्ञं यजमानं सर्वांश् चर्त्विजो ऽभिरक्षति ।
तस्माद् एवंविदम् एव ब्रह्माणं कुर्वीत नानेवंविदं नानेवंविदम् ॥
iast: evaṃvid dha vai brahmā yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ sarvāṃś cartvijo ’bhirakṣati ।
tasmād evaṃvidam eva brahmāṇaṃ kurvīta nānevaṃvidaṃ nānevaṃvidam ॥
words: name of a people of India and of their country (situated near the country of the

tr.text: Just as the mare protects (the soldier), even so the silent Brahman priest is the only priest who protects the people engaged in rituals. The Brahman priest who knows thus verily protects the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and all the priests. Hence one should appoint as a Brahman priest only him who knows thus, not one who does not know thus – yea, not one who does not know thus.

sa: यो ह वै ज्येष्ठं च श्रेष्ठं च वेद ज्येष्ठश् च ह वै श्रेष्ठश् च भवति ।
प्राणो वाव ज्येष्ठश् च श्रेष्ठश् च ॥
iast: yo ha vai jyeṣṭhaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ ca veda jyeṣṭhaś ca ha vai śreṣṭhaś ca bhavati ।
prāṇo vāva jyeṣṭhaś ca śreṣṭhaś ca ॥

tr.text: Om, Verily, he who knows the eldest and the best, surely becomes the eldest and the best. Prana is indeed the eldest and the best (of the organs).

sa: यो ह वै वसिष्ठं वेद वसिष्ठो ह स्वानां भवति ।
iast: yo ha vai vasiṣṭhaṃ veda vasiṣṭho ha svānāṃ bhavati ।

tr.text: Verily, he who knows the richest, becomes the richest among his own people. Speech is indeed the richest.

sa: यो ह वै प्रतिष्ठां वेद प्रति ह तिष्ठत्य् अस्मिंश् च लोके ऽमुष्मिंश् च ।
iast: yo ha vai pratiṣṭhāṃ veda prati ha tiṣṭhaty asmiṃś ca loke ’muṣmiṃś ca ।

tr.text: Verily, he who knows the stable basis, becomes stabilized in this world and in the next. The eye is indeed the stable basis.

sa: यो ह वै संपदं वेद सं हास्मै कामाः पद्यन्ते दैवाश् च मानुषाश् च ।
iast: yo ha vai saṃpadaṃ veda saṃ hāsmai kāmāḥ padyante daivāś ca mānuṣāś ca ।

tr.text: Verily, he who knows prosperity, attains all desires, both divine and human. The ear is indeed prosperity.

sa: यो ह वा आयतनं वेदायतनं ह स्वानां भवति ।
iast: yo ha vā āyatanaṃ vedāyatanaṃ ha svānāṃ bhavati ।

tr.text: Verily, he who knows the abode, becomes the abode of his people. The mind is indeed the abode.

sa: अहं श्रेयान् अस्म्य् अहं श्रेयान् अस्मीति ॥
iast: ahaṃ śreyān asmy ahaṃ śreyān asmīti ॥

tr.text: Now, once the five senses disputed among themselves about their personal superiority, saying ‘I am superior’.

sa: ते ह प्राणाः प्रजापतिं पितरम् एत्योचुः भगवन् को नः श्रेष्ठ इति ।
यस्मिन् व उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं पापिष्ठतरम् इव दृश्येत स वः श्रेष्ठ इति ॥
iast: te ha prāṇāḥ prajāpatiṃ pitaram etyocuḥ bhagavan ko naḥ śreṣṭha iti ।
yasmin va utkrānte śarīraṃ pāpiṣṭhataram iva dṛśyeta sa vaḥ śreṣṭha iti ॥

tr.text: Those senses approached the father Prajapati and said to him, ‘Revered sir, who is the best amongst us ?’ He replied, ‘He amongst you is the best on whose departure the body would appear its worst, as it were.’

sa: यथा कला अवदन्तः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन पश्यन्तश् चक्षुषा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेण ध्यायन्तो मनसैवम् इति ।
iast: yathā kalā avadantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivam iti ।
words: mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)

tr.text: Speech departed. Staying a year out, it came back and asked, ‘How have you been able to live without me ?’ (The others replied,) ‘Just like the dumb, though not speaking, yet living with the breath, seeing with the eyes, hearing with the ear and thinking with the mind.’ (At this) speech entered (the body).

sa: यथान्धा अपश्यन्तः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन वदन्तो वाचा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेण ध्यायन्तो मनसैवम् इति ।
iast: yathāndhā apaśyantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivam iti ।
words: mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)

tr.text: The eye departed. Staying a year out, it came back and asked, ‘How have you been able to live without me ?’ (The others replied,) ‘Just like the blind, though not seeing, yet living with the breath, speaking with the organ of speech, hearing with the ear and thinking with the mind.’ (At this) the eye entered (the body).

sa: तत् संवत्सरं प्रोष्य पर्येत्योवाच कथम् अशकतर्ते मज् जीवितुम् इति ।
यथा बधिरा अशृण्वन्तः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन वदन्तो वाचा पश्यन्तश् चक्षुषा ध्यायन्तो मनसैवम् इति ।
iast: tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣya paryetyovāca katham aśakatarte maj jīvitum iti ।
yathā badhirā aśṛṇvantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā dhyāyanto manasaivam iti ।
words: not hearing or liking to hear
mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)

tr.text: The ear departed. Staying a year out, it came back and asked, ‘How have you been able to live without me ?’ (The others replied,) ‘Just like the deaf, though not hearing, yet living with the breath, speaking with the organ of speech, seeing with the eye and thinking with the mind.’ (At this) the ear entered (the body).

sa: यथा बाला अमनसः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन वदन्तो वाचा पश्यन्तश् चक्षुषा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेणैवम् इति ।
iast: yathā bālā amanasaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇaivam iti ।

tr.text: The mind departed. Staying a year out, it came back and asked, ‘How have you been able to live without me ?’ (The others replied,) ‘Just like infants without developed minds, yet living with the breath, speaking with the organ of speech, seeing with the eye and hearing with the ear.’ (At this) the mind entered (the body).

sa: अथ ह प्राण उच्चिक्रमिषन् स यथा सुहयः पड्वीशशङ्कून् संखिदेद् एवम् इतरान् प्राणान् समखिदत् ।
iast: atha ha prāṇa uccikramiṣan sa yathā suhayaḥ paḍvīśaśaṅkūn saṃkhided evam itarān prāṇān samakhidat ।

tr.text: Then, as the Prana was about to depart, it uprooted the other senses just as a horse of mettle would uproot the pegs to which it is tethered. They all then came to it and said, ‘O revered sir, be our lord, you are the best amongst us; do not depart from the body.’

sa: यद् अहं वसिष्ठो ऽस्मि त्वं तद्वसिष्ठो ऽसीति ।

tr.text: Then speech said to that one, ‘Just as I am the richest, in the same manner are you also the richest’. Then the eye said to that one, ‘Just as I am the stable basis, in the same manner are you also the stable basis’.

sa: यद् अहं संपद् अस्मि त्वं तत्संपद् असीति ।
यद् अहम् आयतनम् अस्मि त्वं तदायतनम् असीति ॥
iast: yad ahaṃ saṃpad asmi tvaṃ tatsaṃpad asīti ।
yad aham āyatanam asmi tvaṃ tadāyatanam asīti ॥

tr.text: Then the ear said to that one, ‘Just as I am prosperity, in the same manner are you also prosperity.’ Then the mind said to that one, ‘Just as I am the abode, in the same manner are you also the abode.’

sa: न वै वाचो न चक्षूंषि न श्रोत्राणि न मनांसीत्य् आचक्षते ।
iast: na vai vāco na cakṣūṃṣi na śrotrāṇi na manāṃsīty ācakṣate ।
words: mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)

tr.text: Verily, people do not call them as organs of speech, nor as eyes, nor as ears, nor as minds. But they call them only as Pranas; for the Prana indeed is all these.

sa: स होवाच किं मे ऽन्नं भविष्यतीति ।
यत् किंचिद् इदम् आ श्वभ्य आ शकुनिभ्य इति होचुः ।
न ह वा एवंविदि किंचनानन्नं भवतीति ॥
iast: yat kiṃcid idam ā śvabhya ā śakunibhya iti hocuḥ ।
na ha vā evaṃvidi kiṃcanānannaṃ bhavatīti ॥
words: a bird (esp. a large bird = gridhra or cilla)

tr.text: He (the Prana) asked, ‘What will be my food?’ ‘Whatever there is here, even (the food) of dogs and birds’, replied the senses. Whatever is eaten, all that is the food of Ana. The name "Ana’ indeed is self-evident. For him who knows thus there is nothing that is not food.

sa: स होवाच किं मे वासो भविष्यतीति ।
तस्माद् वा एतद् अशिष्यन्तः पुरस्ताच् चोपरिष्टाच् चाद्भिः परिदधति ।
iast: sa hovāca kiṃ me vāso bhaviṣyatīti ।
tasmād vā etad aśiṣyantaḥ purastāc copariṣṭāc cādbhiḥ paridadhati ।
words: to lay or put or place or set round

tr.text: He asked, ‘What will be my garments ?’ ‘Water’, replied the senses. Therefore, indeed, those who are about to eat, cover it, both before and after, with water. (He who knows thus) becomes the obtainer of clothes and of upper garments.

sa: तद् धैतत् सत्यकामो जाबालो गोश्रुतये वैयाघ्रपद्यायोक्त्वोवाच ।
यद्य् अप्य् एनच् छुष्काय स्थाणवे ब्रूयाज् जायेरन्न् एवास्मिञ् छाखाः प्ररोहेयुः पलाशानीति ॥
iast: tad dhaitat satyakāmo jābālo gośrutaye vaiyāghrapadyāyoktvovāca ।
yady apy enac chuṣkāya sthāṇave brūyāj jāyerann evāsmiñ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ॥
words: name of a man with the patr. Vaiyāghrapadya

tr.text: Satyakama Jabala imparted this (doctrine of Prana) to Gosruti, the son of Vyaghrapada, and said, ‘If anyone should impart this even to a dry stump, then branches would certainly shoot and leaves would sprout from it’.

sa: अथ यदि महज् जिगमिषेत्, अमावास्यायाम् दीक्षित्वा पौर्णमास्यां रात्रौ सर्वौषधस्य मन्थम् दधिमधुनोर् उपमथ्य ज्येष्ठाय श्रेष्ठाय स्वाहेत्य् अग्नाव् आज्यस्य हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् अवनयेत् ॥
iast: atha yadi mahaj jigamiṣet, amāvāsyāyām dīkṣitvā paurṇamāsyāṃ rātrau sarvauṣadhasya mantham dadhimadhunor upamathya jyeṣṭhāya śreṣṭhāya svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet ॥
words: the night of new moon (when the sun and moon 'dwell together')
to consecrate or dedicate one's self (esp. for the performance of the Soma-sacri
a day or night of full moon
hail! hail to! may a blessing rest on!
to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)
to lead or bring down into (water)

tr.text: Next, if that knower of Prana desires to attain greatness, then having consecrated himself on the new moon day, he should, on the full moon night, stir up in a vessel of curd and honey the mash of all herbs and then offer an oblation into the fire on the spot prescribed for offerings, with the Mantra, ‘Svaha to the eldest and the best’, and throw what remains attached to the ladle into the mash-pot.

sa: वसिष्ठाय स्वाहेत्य् अग्नाव् आज्यस्य हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् अवनयेत् ।
प्रतिष्ठायै स्वाहेत्य् अग्नाव् आज्यस्य हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् अवनयेत् ।
संपदे स्वाहेत्य् अग्नाव् आज्यस्य हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् अवनयेत् ।
आयतनाय स्वाहेत्य् अग्नाव् आज्यस्य हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् अवनयेत् ॥
iast: vasiṣṭhāya svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet ।
pratiṣṭhāyai svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet ।
saṃpade svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet ।
āyatanāya svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet ॥
words: to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)
to lead or bring down into (water)
hail! hail to! may a blessing rest on!
to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)
to lead or bring down into (water)
hail! hail to! may a blessing rest on!
to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)
to lead or bring down into (water)
hail! hail to! may a blessing rest on!
to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)
to lead or bring down into (water)

tr.text: With the Mantra "Svaha to the richest’, he should offer an oblation into the fire on the spot prescribed for offerings, and throw what remains attached to the ladle into the mash-pot. With the Mantra ‘Svaha to what is stable’, he should offer an oblation into the fire on the spot prescribed for offerings, and throw what remains attached to the ladle into the mash-pot. With Mantra ‘Svaha to prosperity’, he should offer an oblation into the fire on the spot prescribed for offerings, and throw what remains attached to the ladle into the mash-pot. With the Mantra ‘Svaha to the abode’, he should offer an oblation into the fire on the spot prescribed for offerings, and throw what remains attached to the ladle into the mash-pot.

sa: स मा ज्यैष्ठ्यं श्रैष्ठ्यं राज्यम् आधिपत्यं गमयतु ।
iast: sa mā jyaiṣṭhyaṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ rājyam ādhipatyaṃ gamayatu ।
words: the open hands placed side by side and slightly hollowed (as if by a beggar to r
to utter in a low voice

tr.text: Then, moving a little away and taking the mash-pot in his hands, he should recite (the Mantra): ‘You are Ama by name, for all this (universe) rests with you. He (i.e. you as Prana) is the eldest, the best, the effulgent, and sovereign. May he (i.e. you as Prana) lead me to the eldest age, to the best position, to effulgence, and to sovereignty. Verily I wish to become all this.’

sa: निर्णिज्य कंसं चमसं वा पश्चाद् अग्नेः संविशति ।
चर्मणि वा स्थण्डिले वा वाचंयमो ऽप्रसाहः ।
स यदि स्त्रियं पश्येत् समृद्धं कर्मेति विद्यात् ॥
iast: nirṇijya kaṃsaṃ camasaṃ vā paścād agneḥ saṃviśati ।
sa yadi striyaṃ paśyet samṛddhaṃ karmeti vidyāt ॥
words: to sip (water) from the palm of the hand for purification
to sip (water) from the palm of the hand for purification
to sip (water) from the palm of the hand for purification
to sip (water) from the palm of the hand for purification
a vessel used at sacrifices for drinking the Soma
an open unoccupied piece of ground

tr.text: Then, reciting this Rik-mantra, foot by foot, he should sip. ‘We pray for that food pertaining to the Progenitor’, saying this (line) he should sip. ‘We pray for the food of the effulgent one’, saying this he should sip. ‘(Which is) the best and all-sustaining’, saying this he should sip. We readily meditate upon (the form of the deity) Bhaga’, saying this and washing the pot shaped like a Kamsa (goblet) or a Camasa (cup), he should drink all. Then he should lie down behind the fire on a skin or on the ground, controlling speech and mind. If he should see a woman (in a dream), he should know that his rite has succeeded.

sa: यदा कर्मसु काम्येषु स्त्रियं स्वप्नेषु पश्यति ।
समृद्धिं तत्र जानीयात् तस्मिन् स्वप्ननिदर्शने तस्मिन् स्वप्ननिदर्शने ॥
iast: yadā karmasu kāmyeṣu striyaṃ svapneṣu paśyati ।
samṛddhiṃ tatra jānīyāt tasmin svapnanidarśane tasmin svapnanidarśane ॥

tr.text: There is this verse about it: During the performance of the rites for desired results if the performer sees a woman in a dream, then he should recognize fulfilment in this vision in a dream – yea, in this vision in a dream.
Once Svetaketu, the grandson of Aruna, came to the assembly of the Panchalas. Pravahana, the son of Jivala, enquired of him, ‘My boy, has your father instructed you ?’ ‘He has indeed, revered sir’.

sa: वेत्थ यद् इतो ऽधि प्रजाः प्रयन्तीति ।
वेत्थ पथोर् देवयानस्य पितृयाणस्य च व्यावर्तना ३ इति ।
iast: vettha pathor devayānasya pitṛyāṇasya ca vyāvartanā 3 iti ।

tr.text: ‘Do you know where created beings go above from here ?’ No, revered sir’. ‘Do you know the place of parting of the two paths – the path of the gods and the path of the fathers ?’ ‘No, revered sir’.

sa: वेत्थ यथासौ लोको न संपूर्यत ३ इति ।
वेत्थ यथा पञ्चम्याम् आहुताव् आपः पुरुषवचसो भवन्तीति ।
iast: vettha yathāsau loko na saṃpūryata 3 iti ।
vettha yathā pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavantīti ।

tr.text: ‘Do you know why the other world is not filled up ?’ ‘No, revered sir’. ‘Do you know how, at the fifth oblation, the liquid oblations (or unseen results of action) come to be designated as man ?’ ‘No, indeed, revered sir’.

sa: अथानु किम् अनु शिष्ठो ऽवोचथा यो हीमानि न विद्यात् ।
तं होवाचाननुशिष्य वाव किल मा भगवान् अब्रवीद् अनु त्वाशिषम् इति ॥
iast: athānu kim anu śiṣṭho ’vocathā yo hīmāni na vidyāt ।
taṃ hovācānanuśiṣya vāva kila mā bhagavān abravīd anu tvāśiṣam iti ॥

tr.text: ’Then why did you say, "I have been instructed" ? Foz, how can he who does not know these things say, "I have been instructed" ?’ He was distressed and came to his father’s place and said to him, ‘Revered Sir, wiuhout having instructed me properly you said, "I have instructed you".’

sa: स होवाच यथा मा त्वं तदैतान् अवदो यथाहम् एषां नैकंचन वेद ।
यद्य् अहम् इमान् अवेदिष्यं कथं ते नावक्ष्यम् इति ॥
iast: sa hovāca yathā mā tvaṃ tadaitān avado yathāham eṣāṃ naikaṃcana veda ।
yady aham imān avediṣyaṃ kathaṃ te nāvakṣyam iti ॥

tr.text: ‘That nominal Kshatriya asked me five questions, and I was not able to answer even one of them’. The father said, ‘Even as you have spoken to me about them, so do I not know even one of them. If I had known them, why should I not have toll you ?’

sa: स ह गौतमो राज्ञो ऽर्धम् एयाय ।
मानुषस्य भगवन् गौतम वित्तस्य वरं वृणीथा इति ।
याम् एव कुमारस्यान्ते वाचम् अभाषथास् ताम् एव मे ब्रूहीति ।
iast: mānuṣasya bhagavan gautama vittasya varaṃ vṛṇīthā iti ।
yām eva kumārasyānte vācam abhāṣathās tām eva me brūhīti ।

tr.text: Then Gautama went to the king’s place. When he arrived, the king made reverential offerings to him. In the morning he presented himself to the king when he was in the assembly. The king said to him, ‘O revered Gautama, please ask for a boon of human wealth’. He replied, ‘O king, let the human wealth remain with you, tell me those words which you spoke to my boy’. The king was perturbed.

sa: तं ह चिरं वसेत्य् आज्ञापयां चकार ।
यथेयं न प्राक् त्वत्तः पुरा विद्या ब्राह्मणान् गच्छति ।
तस्माद् उ सर्वेषु लोकेषु क्षत्रस्यैव प्रशासनम् अभूद् इति ।
iast: taṃ ha ciraṃ vasety ājñāpayāṃ cakāra ।
yatheyaṃ na prāk tvattaḥ purā vidyā brāhmaṇān gacchati ।
tasmād u sarveṣu lokeṣu kṣatrasyaiva praśāsanam abhūd iti ।

tr.text: The king commanded him, ‘Stay here for a long time.’ At the end of the period he said to him, ‘Even as you told me, O Gautama, prior to you, this knowledge never went to the Brahmanas. This is why the expounding of this knowledge belonged to the Kshatriyas in earlier times in all the worlds’. Then he instructed him.
The world yonder is indeed the fire, O Gautama. Of that, the sun is the fuel, the rays are the smoke, the day is the flame, the moon is the embers, and the stars are the sparks.

sa: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवाः श्रद्धां जुह्वति ।
iast: tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ śraddhāṃ juhvati ।

tr.text: Into this fire the deities offer the oblation of faith. Out of that oblation King Soma arises.
Parjanya is indeed the fire, O Gautama. Of that, the air is the fuel, the cloud is the smoke, the lightning is the flame, the thunderbolt is the embers, and the rumblings of thunder are the sparks.

sa: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवाः सोमं राजानं जुह्वति ।
iast: tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ somaṃ rājānaṃ juhvati ।

tr.text: Into this fire the deities offer the oblation of King Soma. Out of that oblation rain arises.
The earth indeed is the fire, O Gautama. Of that, the year, is the fuel, Akasa is the smgke, night is the flame, the directions are the embers, and the intermediate directions are the sparks.

sa: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवा वर्षं जुह्वति ।
iast: tasminn etasminn agnau devā varṣaṃ juhvati ।

tr.text: Into this fire the deities offer the oblation of rain. Out of that oblation food (in the shape of corn) arises.
Man indeed is the fire, O Gautama. Of that, speech is the fuel, Prana is the smoke, the tongue is the flame, the eye is the embers, and the ear is the sparks.

sa: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवा अन्नं जुह्वति ।
iast: tasminn etasminn agnau devā annaṃ juhvati ।

tr.text: Into this fire the deities offer the oblation of food. Out of that oblation the seed arises.
Woman indeed is the fire, O Gautama. Into this fire the deities offer the oblation of the seed. Out of that oblation the foetus arises.

sa: तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् अग्नौ देवा रेतो जुह्वति ।
iast: tasminn etasminn agnau devā reto juhvati ।

tr.text: Woman indeed is the fire, O Gautama. Into this fire the deities offer the oblation of the seed. Out of that oblation the foetus arises.

sa: इति तु पञ्चम्याम् आहुताव् आपः पुरुषवचसो भवन्तीति ।
स उल्बावृतो गर्भो दश वा नव वा मासान् अन्तः शयित्वा यावद् वाथ जायते ॥
iast: iti tu pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavantīti ।
sa ulbāvṛto garbho daśa vā nava vā māsān antaḥ śayitvā yāvad vātha jāyate ॥

tr.text: Thus at the fifth oblation, (the oblation called) water comes to be designated as man. That foetus, covered with membrane, lies for nine or ten months, and is then born.

sa: तं प्रेतं दिष्टम् इतो ऽग्नय एव हरन्ति यत एवेतो यतः संभूतो भवति ॥
iast: taṃ pretaṃ diṣṭam ito ’gnaya eva haranti yata eveto yataḥ saṃbhūto bhavati ॥

tr.text: Being born, he lives whatever the length of his life may be. When he is dead (to attain the world) as ordained, they carry him from here (for cremation) to fire itself from which alone he came and from which he arose.

sa: ये चेमे ऽरण्ये श्रद्धा तप इत्य् उपासते ।
आपूर्यमाणपक्षाद् यान् षड् उदङ्ङ् एति मासांस् तान् ॥
iast: ye ceme ’raṇye śraddhā tapa ity upāsate ।
āpūryamāṇapakṣād yān ṣaḍ udaṅṅ eti māsāṃs tān ॥

tr.text: Among them, those who know thus (this knowledge of the five fires) and those who are devoted to faith and austerity in the forest – they go to light; from light to the day, from the day to the bright fortnight, from the bright fortnight to those six months during which the sun travels northward; from the months to the year, from the year to the sun, from the sun to the moon and from the moon to the lightning. (From the region of Brahman) a person, who is other than human, (comes and) causes them, existing there, to attain Brahman. This is the path of the gods.

Among them, those who know thus (this knowledge of the five fires) and those who are devoted to faith and austerity in the forest – they go to light; from light to the day, from the day to the bright fortnight, from the bright fortnight to those six months during which the sun travels northward; from the months to the year, from the year to the sun, from the sun to the moon and from the moon to the lightning. (From the region of Brahman) a person, who is other than human, (comes and) causes them, existing there, to attain Brahman. This is the path of the gods.

sa: अथ य इमे ग्राम इष्टापूर्ते दत्तम् इत्य् उपासते ।
अपरपक्षाद् यान् षड् दक्षिणैति मासांस् तान् ।
iast: atha ya ime grāma iṣṭāpūrte dattam ity upāsate ।
aparapakṣād yān ṣaḍ dakṣiṇaiti māsāṃs tān ।

tr.text: But those who living in villages (as householders) practise sacrifices and works of public utility and gift, go to smoke, from smoke to night, from night to the dark fortnight, from the dark fortnight to those months during which the sun travels southward. From there they do not reach the year (like those going the path of the gods).

From the months, (they go) to the region of the fathers, from the region of the fathers to Akasa, from Akasa to the moon. This (i.e. this moon) is King Soma (the king of the Brahmanas). This is the food of the deities. This the deities eat.

sa: तस्मिन् यवात्संपातम् उषित्वाथैतम् एवाध्वानं पुनर् निवर्तन्ते ।
iast: tasmin yavātsaṃpātam uṣitvāthaitam evādhvānaṃ punar nivartante ।

tr.text: Residing in that (region of the moon) till they have exhausted (the results of action) they then return again the same way as they came (by the path that is being mentioned). They come to Akasa, and from Akasa to air. Having become air, they become smoke. Having become smoke they become the white cloud.

sa: त इह व्रीहियवा ओषधिवनस्पतयस् तिलमासा इति जायन्ते ऽतो वै खलु दुर्निष्प्रपतरम् ।
यो यो ह्य् अन्नम् अत्ति यो रेतः सिञ्चति तद् भूय एव भवति ॥
iast: ta iha vrīhiyavā oṣadhivanaspatayas tilamāsā iti jāyante ’to vai khalu durniṣprapataram ।
yo yo hy annam atti yo retaḥ siñcati tad bhūya eva bhavati ॥

tr.text: Having become the white cloud, they become the (rain-bearing) cloud. Having become the cloud they fall as rain. Then they are born in this world as rice and barley, herbs and trees, sesamum plants and beans. But the release from these is more difficult, for whoever eats the food and sows the seed, they become like him only.

sa: तद् य इह रमणीयचरणा अभ्याशो ह यत् ते रमणीयां योनिम् आपद्येरन् ब्राह्मणयोनिं वा क्षत्रिययोनिं वा वैश्ययोनिं वा ।
अथ य इह कपूयचरणा अभ्याशो ह यत् ते कपूयां योनिम् आपद्येरञ् श्वयोनिम् वा सूकरयोनिं वा चण्डालयोनिं वा ॥
iast: tad ya iha ramaṇīyacaraṇā abhyāśo ha yat te ramaṇīyāṃ yonim āpadyeran brāhmaṇayoniṃ vā kṣatriyayoniṃ vā vaiśyayoniṃ vā ।
atha ya iha kapūyacaraṇā abhyāśo ha yat te kapūyāṃ yonim āpadyerañ śvayonim vā sūkarayoniṃ vā caṇḍālayoniṃ vā ॥

tr.text: Among them, those who have good residual results of action here (earned in this world and left as residue after the enjoyment in the region of the moon), quickly reach a good womb, the womb of a Brahmana, or of a Kshatriya or of a Vaisya. But those who have bad residual results of action quickly reach an evil womb, the womb of a dog or of a hog or of a Chandala.

sa: अथैतयोः पथोर् न कतरेणचन तानीमानि क्षुद्राण्य् असकृदावर्तीनि भूतानि भवन्ति जायस्व म्रियस्वेति ।
iast: athaitayoḥ pathor na katareṇacana tānīmāni kṣudrāṇy asakṛdāvartīni bhūtāni bhavanti jāyasva mriyasveti ।

tr.text: Then, by neither of these two paths, do they go. They, as small creatures, keep repeatedly revolving, subject to the saying ‘Be born and die’. This is the third state. Therefore that region (of the moon) is never filled up. Hence one should be disgusted (with this state). There is this verse about it.

sa: एते पतन्ति चत्वारः पञ्चमश् चाचरंस् तैर् इति ॥
iast: ete patanti catvāraḥ pañcamaś cācaraṃs tair iti ॥

tr.text: One who steals gold, one who drinks wine, one who dishonours the teacher’s bed, and one who injures a Brahmana – all these four fall, as also the fifth one who associates with them.

sa: अथ ह य एतान् एवं पञ्चाग्नीन् वेद न सह तैर् अप्य् आचरन् पाप्मना लिप्यते ।
शुद्धः पूतः पुण्यलोको भवति य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ॥
iast: atha ha ya etān evaṃ pañcāgnīn veda na saha tair apy ācaran pāpmanā lipyate ।
śuddhaḥ pūtaḥ puṇyaloko bhavati ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: Moreover, he who knows (worships) these five fires thus, even though he associates with those sinners, is not tainted by sin. He who knows these thus becomes cleansed and pure and obtains the meritorious world – yea, he who knows thus.

sa: प्राचीनशाल औपमन्यवः सत्ययज्ञः पौलुषिर् इन्द्रद्युम्नो भाल्लवेयो जनः शार्कराक्ष्यो बुडिल आश्वतराश्विस् ते हैते महाशाला महाश्रोत्रियाः समेत्य मीमांसां चक्रुः ।
iast: prācīnaśāla aupamanyavaḥ satyayajñaḥ pauluṣir indradyumno bhāllaveyo janaḥ śārkarākṣyo buḍila āśvatarāśvis te haite mahāśālā mahāśrotriyāḥ sametya mīmāṃsāṃ cakruḥ ।
words: a Brāhman versed in the Veda
profound thought or reflection or Consideration

tr.text: Pracinasala the son of Upamanyu, Satyayajna the son of Pulusa, Indradyumna the son of Bhallavi, Jana the son of Sarkaraksa, and Budila the son of Asvatarasva – these five great householders and great Vedic scholars, having come together, held a discussion on ‘What is our Atman ? What is Brahman ?’

sa: उद्दालको वै भगवन्तो ऽयम् आरुणिः संप्रतीमम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् अध्येति ।
iast: uddālako vai bhagavanto ’yam āruṇiḥ saṃpratīmam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram adhyeti ।
words: name of Uddālaka (a renowned Brāhmaṇa teacher)

tr.text: They reflected among themselves, ‘Revered sirs, Uddalaka, the son of Aruna, knows well this Vaisvanara Atman. Well, let us go to him’. And they went to him.

words: a Brāhman versed in the Veda
an exclamation or inceptive particle (expressive of an exhortation to do anythin

tr.text: Uddalaka reflected, ‘These great householders and great Vedic scholars are going to uestion me; but possibly I shall not be able to tell them everything. However, I shall direct them to another teacher’.

sa: अश्वपतिर् वै भगवन्तो ऽयं कैकेयः संप्रतीमम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् अध्येति ।
iast: aśvapatir vai bhagavanto ’yaṃ kaikeyaḥ saṃpratīmam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram adhyeti ।

tr.text: Uddalaka said to the, ‘Revered sirs, at present, Asvapati, the son of Kekaya, is studying this Vaisvanara Atman. Well, let us go to him’. Then they went to him.

sa: तेभ्यो ह प्राप्तेभ्यः पृथग् अर्हाणि कारयां चकार ।
न मे स्तेनो जनपदे न कदर्यो न मद्यपः ।
नानाहिताग्निर् नाविद्वान् न स्वैरी स्वैरिणी कुतः ।
यावद् एकैकस्मा ऋत्विजे धनं दास्यामि तावद् भगवद्भ्यो दास्यामि ।
iast: tebhyo ha prāptebhyaḥ pṛthag arhāṇi kārayāṃ cakāra ।
na me steno janapade na kadaryo na madyapaḥ ।
nānāhitāgnir nāvidvān na svairī svairiṇī kutaḥ ।
yāvad ekaikasmā ṛtvije dhanaṃ dāsyāmi tāvad bhagavadbhyo dāsyāmi ।
words: one who has not performed the Agnyādhāna
the prize of a contest or the contest itself (lit. a running match)

tr.text: When they arrived, the king arranged for each of them separately a welcome with suitable rites. Next morning, on rising, he said to them, ‘In my kingdom there is no thief, no miser, no drunkard, no man who has not installed the fire, no ignorant person, no adulterer, so how can there be any adulteress ? Revered sirs, I am going to perform a sacrifice. In that as much wealth, sirs, as I give to each single priest, shall I give to you also. Revered sirs, please remain’.

sa: येन हैवार्थेन पुरुषश् चरेत् तं हैव वदेत् ।
iast: yena haivārthena puruṣaś caret taṃ haiva vadet ।

tr.text: They said, ‘The purpose for which a man goes (to another), on that alone he should speak to him. You are, at present, studying the Vaisvanara Atman, please tell us of that.

words: the earlier part of the day

tr.text: The king said to them, ‘I shall answer you in the morning’. In the morning, they approached him with sacrificial fuel in their hands. The king, without receiving them as initiated pupils, spoke thus:

sa: औपमन्यव कं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्स इति ।
दिवम् एव भगवो राजन्न् इति होवाच ।
एष वै सुतेजा आत्मा वैश्वानरो यं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्से ।
तस्मात् तव सुतं प्रसुतम् आसुतं कुले दृश्यते ॥
iast: aupamanyava kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti ।
divam eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca ।
eṣa vai sutejā ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse ।
tasmāt tava sutaṃ prasutam āsutaṃ kule dṛśyate ॥
words: the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)

tr.text: ‘O Aupamanyava, what is the Atman on which you meditate ?’ He replied, ‘Heaven only, O venerable king’. The king said, ‘This that you meditate upon as Atman is the Vaisvanara Atman known as "the highly luminous". Therefore in your family are seen the Suta, Prasuta and Asuta libations of Soma-juice.’

sa: अत्त्य् अन्नं पश्यति प्रियम् भवत्य् अस्य ब्रह्मवर्चसं कुले ये एतम् एवम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् उपास्ते ।
मूधा त्व् एष आत्मन इति होवाच ।
मूर्धा ते व्यपतिष्यद् यन् मां नागमिष्य इति ॥
iast: atty annaṃ paśyati priyam bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ye etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste ।
mūdhā tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca ।
mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti ॥
words: to fly or dash or rush through

tr.text: ‘So you eat food and see what is dear. One who meditates on this Vaisvanara Atman thus, eats food and sees what is dear, and there is in his family the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom. But this is only the head of the Atman. If you had not come to me your head (a portion) would have fallen down.’

sa: प्राचीनयोग्य कं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्स इति ।
आदित्यम् एव भगवो राजन्न् इति होवाच ।
एष वै विश्वरूप आत्मा वैश्वानरो यं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्ते ।
तस्मात् तव बहु विश्वरूपं कुले दृश्यते ॥
iast: prācīnayogya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti ।
ādityam eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca ।
eṣa vai viśvarūpa ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāste ।
tasmāt tava bahu viśvarūpaṃ kule dṛśyate ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: Then the king said to Satyayajna Paulusi, ‘O Pracinayogya, what is that Atman on which you meditate ?’ He replied, ‘The sun only, O venerable king’. The king said, ‘This that you meditate upon as Atman is the Vaisvanara Atman known as "the multiform". Therefore in your family are seen all kinds of enjoyable things.

sa: अत्त्य् अन्नं पश्यति प्रियं भवत्य् अस्य ब्रह्मवर्चसं कुले य एतम् एवम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् उपास्ते ।
चक्षुष् ट्व् एतद् आत्मन इति होवाच ।
अन्धो ऽभविष्यो यन् मां नागमिष्य इति ॥
iast: atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste ।
cakṣuṣ ṭv etad ātmana iti hovāca ।
words: to roll or go onwards (as a carriage)
a golden ornament for the neck or breast

tr.text: ‘So, for you are provided a chariot drawn by mules, maid-servants and a gold necklace; so you eat food and see what is dear. One who thus meditates upon this Vaisvanara Atman, eats food and sees what is dear, and there is in his family the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom. But this is only the eye of the Atman. If you had not come to me you would have become blind.’

sa: वैयाघ्रपद्य कं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्स इति ।
वायुम् एव भगवो राजन्न् इति होवाच ।
एष वै पृथग्वर्त्मात्मा वैश्वानरो यं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्से ।
तस्मात् त्वां पृथग् बलय आयन्ति पृथग् रथश्रेणयो ऽनुयन्ति ॥
iast: vaiyāghrapadya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti ।
vāyum eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca ।
eṣa vai pṛthagvartmātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse ।
tasmāt tvāṃ pṛthag balaya āyanti pṛthag rathaśreṇayo ’nuyanti ॥
words: the track or rut of a wheel

tr.text: Then the king said to Indradyumna Bhallaveya, ‘O descendant of Vyaghrapada, what is that Atman on which you meditate ?’ He replied, ‘Air only, O venerable king.’ The king said, ‘This that you meditate upon as Atman is the Vaisvanara Atman known as "the diversely coursed". Therefore from diverse directions offerings come to you, and various rows of chariots follow you.

sa: अत्त्य् अन्नं पश्यति प्रियं भवत्य् अस्य ब्रह्मवर्चसं कुले य एतम् एवम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् उपास्ते ।
प्राणस् त्व् एष आत्मन इति होवाच ।
प्राणस् त उदक्रमिष्यद् यन् मां नागमिष्य इति ॥
iast: atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste ।
prāṇas tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca ।
prāṇas ta udakramiṣyad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti ॥

tr.text: ‘So you eat food and see what is dear. One who thus meditates upon this Vaisvanara Atman eats food and sees what is dear, and there is in his family the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom. But this is only the Prana of the Atman. If you had not come to me your Prana would have departed’.

sa: शार्कराक्ष्य कं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्स इति ।
आकाशम् एव भगवो राजन्न् इति होवाच ।
एष वै बहुल आत्मा वैश्वानरो यं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपस्से ।
तस्मात् त्वं बहुलो ऽसि प्रजया च धनेन च ॥
iast: śārkarākṣya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti ।
ākāśam eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca ।
eṣa vai bahula ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upasse ।
tasmāt tvaṃ bahulo ’si prajayā ca dhanena ca ॥
words: the prize of a contest or the contest itself (lit. a running match)

tr.text: Then the king said to Jana, ‘O Sarkaraksya, what is that Atman on which you meditate ?’ He replied, ‘Akasa only, O venerable king’. The king said, ‘This that you meditate upon as Atman is the Vaisvanara Atman known as "the manifold". Therefore are your offspring and wealth manifold.

sa: अत्त्य् अन्नं पश्यति प्रियं भवत्य् अस्य ब्रह्मवर्चसं कुले य एतम् एवम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् उपास्ते ।
संदेहस् त्व् एष आत्मन इति होवाच ।
संदेहस् ते व्यशीर्यद् यन् मां नागमिष्य इति ॥
iast: atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste ।
saṃdehas tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca ।
saṃdehas te vyaśīryad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti ॥

a conglomeration or conglutination (of material elements)

tr.text: ‘So you eat food and see what is dear. One who thus meditates upon this Vaisvanara Atman, eats food and sees what is dear, and there is in his family the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom. But this is only the trunk of the Atman. If you had not come to me your trunk would have been shattered’.

sa: वैयाघ्रपद्य कं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्स इति ।
अप एव भगवो राजन्न् इति होवाच ।
एष वै रयिर् आत्मा वैश्वानरो यं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्से ।
iast: vaiyāghrapadya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti ।
apa eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca ।
eṣa vai rayir ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse ।

tr.text: Then the king said to Budila Asvatarasvi, ‘O Vaiyaghrapadya, what is that Atman on which you meditate ?’ He replied, ‘Water only, O venerable king’. The king said, ‘This that you meditate upon as Atman is the Vaisvanara Atman known as "the wealth". Therefore are you endowed with wealth and bodily strength.

sa: अत्त्य् अन्नं पश्यति प्रियं भवत्य् अस्य ब्रह्मवर्चसं कुले य एतम् एवम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् उपास्ते ।
बस्तिस् त्व् एष आत्मन इति होवाच ।
बस्तिस् ते व्यभेत्स्यद् यन् मां नागमिष्य इति ॥
iast: atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste ।
bastis tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca ।
bastis te vyabhetsyad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti ॥

tr.text: ‘So you eat food and see what is dear. One who thus meditates upon this Vaisvanara Atman, eats food and sees what is dear, and there is in his family the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom. But this is only the lower belly of the Atman. If you had not come to me your lower belly would have burst’.

sa: गौतम कं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपस्स इति ।
पृथिवीम् एव भगवो राजन्न् इति होवाच ।
एष वै प्रतिष्ठात्मा वैश्वानरो यं त्वम् आत्मानम् उपास्से ।
तस्मात् त्वं प्रतिष्ठितो ऽसि प्रजया च पशुभिश् च ॥
iast: gautama kaṃ tvam ātmānam upassa iti ।
pṛthivīm eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca ।
eṣa vai pratiṣṭhātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse ।
tasmāt tvaṃ pratiṣṭhito ’si prajayā ca paśubhiś ca ॥
words: name of Uddālaka (a renowned Brāhmaṇa teacher)

tr.text: Then the king said to Uddalaka Aruni, ‘O Gautama, what is that Atman on which you meditate ?’ He replied, ‘The earth only, O venerable king’. The king said, ‘This that you meditate upon as Atman is the Vaisvanara Atman known as "the foundation". Therefore are you well-founded in offspring and cattle’.

sa: अत्त्य् अन्नं पश्यति प्रियं भवत्य् अस्य ब्रह्मवर्चसं कुले य एतम् एवम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् उपास्ते ।
पादौ त्व् एताव् आत्मन इति होवाच ।
पादौ ते व्यम्लास्येतां यन् मां नागमिष्य इति ॥
iast: atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste ।
pādau tv etāv ātmana iti hovāca ।
pādau te vyamlāsyetāṃ yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti ॥

tr.text: ‘So you eat food and see what is dear. One who thus meditates upon this Vaisvanara Atman, eats food and sees what is dear, and there is in his family the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom. But this is only the feet of the Atman. If you had not come to me your feet would have withered away’.

sa: एते वै खलु यूयं पृथग् इवेमम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरं विद्वांसो ऽन्नम् अत्थ ।
यस् त्व् एतम् एवं प्रादेशमात्रम् अभिविमानम् आत्मानं वैश्वानरम् उपास्ते ।
स सर्वेषु लोकेषु सर्वेषु भूतेषु सर्वेष्व् आत्मस्व् अन्नम् अत्ति ॥
iast: ete vai khalu yūyaṃ pṛthag ivemam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vidvāṃso ’nnam attha ।
yas tv etam evaṃ prādeśamātram abhivimānam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste ।
sa sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣv ātmasv annam atti ॥
words: the span of the thumb and forefinger
endowed with the faculty called abhimāna ("self-reference")

tr.text: The king said to them, ‘All of you (with partial knowledge) eat food knowing the Vaisvanara Atman differently, as it were. But one who thus meditates upon this Vaisvanara Atman as a whole, consisting of parts and self-conscious, eats food in all the worlds, in all the beings, and in all the selves.

sa: तस्य ह वा एतस्यात्मनो वैश्वानरस्य मूर्धैव सुतेजाश् चक्षुर् विश्वरूपः प्राणः पृथग्वर्त्मात्मा संदेहो बहुलो बस्तिर् एव रयिः पृथिव्य् एव पादाव् उर एव वेदिर् लोमाणि बर्हिर् हृदयं गार्हपत्यो मनो ऽन्वाहार्यपचन आस्यम् आहवनीयः ॥
iast: tasya ha vā etasyātmano vaiśvānarasya mūrdhaiva sutejāś cakṣur viśvarūpaḥ prāṇaḥ pṛthagvartmātmā saṃdeho bahulo bastir eva rayiḥ pṛthivy eva pādāv ura eva vedir lomāṇi barhir hṛdayaṃ gārhapatyo mano ’nvāhāryapacana āsyam āhavanīyaḥ ॥

tr.text: Of the aforesaid Vaisvanara Atman, the head is ‘the highly luminous’, the eye is ‘the multiform’, the breath is ‘the diversely coursed’, the trunk is ‘the vast’, the lower belly is the ‘wealth’, the feet are the earth (‘the foundation’). (Of the enjoyer as Vaisvanara) the chest is the altar, the hairs on the chest are the Kusa grass, the heart is the Garhapatya fire, the mind is the Anvaharyapacana fire, and the mouth is the Ahavaniya fire.

sa: तद् यद् भक्तं प्रथमम् आगच्छेत् तद् धोमीयम् ।
स यां प्रथमाम् आहुतिं जुहुयात् तां जुहुयात् प्राणाय स्वाहेति ।
iast: tad yad bhaktaṃ prathamam āgacchet tad dhomīyam ।
sa yāṃ prathamām āhutiṃ juhuyāt tāṃ juhuyāt prāṇāya svāheti ।
words: relating or belonging to or fit or destined for an oblation or sacrifice
offering oblations with fire to the deities
to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)
to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)
hail! hail to! may a blessing rest on!

tr.text: Therefore, the food that comes first should be an object of oblation. That eater, when he offers the first oblation, should offer it with the Mantra ‘Svaha to Prana’; thereby Prana is satisfied.

sa: दिवि तृप्यन्त्यां यत् किंच द्यौश् चादित्यश् चाधितिष्ठतस् तत् तृप्यति ।
तस्यानु तृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिर् अन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति ॥
iast: divi tṛpyantyāṃ yat kiṃca dyauś cādityaś cādhitiṣṭhatas tat tṛpyati ।
tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere

tr.text: Prana being satisfied, the eye is satisfied; the eye being satisfied, the sun is satisfied; the sun being satisfied, heaven is satisfied; heaven being satisfied, whatever is under heaven and the sun is satisfied. Through its satisfaction the eater himself is satisfied. (He is satisfied) also with offspring, cattle, food, lustre and the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom.

sa: अथ यां द्वितीयां जुहुयात् तां जुहुयाद् व्यानाय स्वाहेति ।

tr.text: Then, when he offers the second oblation, he should offer it with the Mantra ‘Svaha to Vyana’; thereby Vyana is satisfied.

sa: दिक्षु तृप्यन्तीषु यत् किंच दिशश् चन्द्रमाश् चाधितिष्ठन्ति तत् तृप्यति ।
तस्यानु तृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिर् अन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति ॥

tr.text: Vyana being satisfied, the ear is satisfied; the ear being satisfied, the moon is satisfied; the moon being satisfied, the quarters are satisfied; the quarters being satisfied, whatever is under the moon and the quarters is satisfied. Through its satisfaction the eater himself is satisfied. (He is satisfied) also with offspring, cattle, food, lustre and the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom.

tr.text: Then, when he offers the third oblation, he should offer it with the Mantra ‘Svaha to Apana’; thereby Apana is satisfied.

tasyānutṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti ॥

Through its satisfaction the eater himself is satisfied. (He is satisfied) also with offspring, cattle, food, lustre and the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom.

sa: अथ यां चतुर्थीं जुहुयात् तां जुहुयात् समानाय स्वाहेति ।
iast: atha yāṃ caturthīṃ juhuyāt tāṃ juhuyāt samānāya svāheti ।

tr.text: Then, when he offers the fourth oblation, he should offer it with the Mantra ‘Svaha to Samana’; thereby Samana is satisfied.

sa: विद्युति तृप्यन्त्यां यत् किं च विद्युच् च  पर्जन्यश् चाधितिष्ठतस् तत् तृप्यति ।
तस्यानु तृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिर् अन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति ॥

tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti ॥

mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)
mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)
a flashing thunderbolt (as the weapon of the Maruts)
a flashing thunderbolt (as the weapon of the Maruts)
a flashing thunderbolt (as the weapon of the Maruts)

tr.text: Samana being satisfied, the mind is satisfied; the mind being satisfied, Parjanya (rain god) is satisfied; Parjanya being satisfied, lightning is satisfied; lightning being satisfied, whatever is under lightning and Parjanya is satisfied. Through its satisfaction the eater himself is satisfied. (He is satisfied) also with offspring, cattle, food, lustre and the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom.

sa: अथ याम् पञ्चमीं जुहुयात् तां जुहुयात् उदानाय स्वाहेति ।

tr.text: Then, when he offers the fifth oblation, he should offer it with the Mantra ‘Svaha to Udana’; thereby Udana is satisfied.

sa: उदाने तृप्यति त्वक् तृप्यति त्वचि तृप्यन्त्यां वायुस् तृप्यति ।
आकाशे तृप्यति यत् किंच वायुश् चाकाशश् चाधितिष्ठतस् तत् तृप्यति ।
तस्यानु तृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिर् अन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति ॥
iast: udāne tṛpyati tvak tṛpyati tvaci tṛpyantyāṃ vāyus tṛpyati ।
ākāśe tṛpyati yat kiṃca vāyuś cākāśaś cādhitiṣṭhatas tat tṛpyati ।
tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti ॥
words: the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)

tr.text: Udana being satisfied, the skin is satisfied; the skin being satisfied, the air is satisfied; the air being satisfied, Akasa is satisfied; Akasa being satisfied, whatever is under the air and Akasa is satisfied. Through its satisfaction the eater himself is satisfied. (He is satisfied) also with offspring, cattle, food, lustre and the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom.

sa: स य इदम् अविद्वान् अग्निहोत्रं जुहोति यथाङ्गारान् अपोह्य भस्मनि जुहुयात् तादृक् तत् स्यात् ॥
iast: sa ya idam avidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti yathāṅgārān apohya bhasmani juhuyāt tādṛk tat syāt ॥
words: to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)
to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)

tr.text: If anyone, without knowing this, offers the Agnihotra, it would be just a man removing the live embers and pouring the oblation on the ashes.

sa: अथ य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अग्निहोत्रं जुहोति तस्य सर्वेषु लोकेषु सर्वेषु भूतेषु सर्वेष्व् आत्मसु हुतं भवति ॥
iast: atha ya etad evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti tasya sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣv ātmasu hutaṃ bhavati ॥
words: to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)
to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)

tr.text: But if one, knowing it thus, offers the Agnihotra to Prana his oblation is poured into all the worlds, all the beings, and all the selves.

sa: तद् यथेषीकातूलम् अग्नौ प्रोतं प्रदूयेतैवं हास्य सर्वे पाप्मानः प्रदूयन्ते य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अग्निहोत्रं जुहोति ॥
iast: tad yatheṣīkātūlam agnau protaṃ pradūyetaivaṃ hāsya sarve pāpmānaḥ pradūyante ya etad evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti ॥
words: to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)

tr.text: So, even as reed-cotton when laid on the fire is burnt up, so are burnt up all the sins of this one who knowing it thus offers the Agnihotra.

sa: तस्माद् उ हैवंविद् यद्य् अपि चण्डालाय उच्छिष्टं प्रयच्छेत् ।
आत्मनि हैवास्य तद् वैश्वानरे हुतं स्याद् इति ।
iast: tasmād u haivaṃvid yady api caṇḍālāya ucchiṣṭaṃ prayacchet ।
ātmani haivāsya tad vaiśvānare hutaṃ syād iti ।
words: to sacrifice (esp. pour butter into the fire)

tr.text: Therefore, even if one, who knows thus, offers the remnant of his food to a Chandala, then also that food becomes his offering to the Vaisvanara Atman only. There is this verse about it.
As, in this world, hungry boys gather round their mother, even so all the creatures wait upon the Agnihotra.

sa: तं ह पितोवाच श्वेतकेतो वस ब्रह्मचर्यम् ।
न वै सोम्यास्मत् कुलीनो ऽननूच्य ब्रह्मबन्धुर् इव भवतीति ॥
iast: taṃ ha pitovāca śvetaketo vasa brahmacaryam ।
na vai somyāsmat kulīno ’nanūcya brahmabandhur iva bhavatīti ॥

tr.text: Om. Once upon a time there was one Svetaketu, the grandson of Aruna. His father said to him, ‘O Svetaketu, live the life of a Brahmacharin. Dear boy, there never is anyone in our family who does not study and is only nominally a Brahmana.’

sa: स ह द्वादशवर्ष उपेत्य चतुर्विंशतिवर्षः सर्वान् वेदान् अधीत्य महामना अनूचानमानी स्तब्ध एयाय ।
iast: sa ha dvādaśavarṣa upetya caturviṃśativarṣaḥ sarvān vedān adhītya mahāmanā anūcānamānī stabdha eyāya ।

tr.text: Having gone (to the teacher’s house) when twelve years old, he came back when he was twenty-four old, having studied all the Vedas, conceited, arrogant and regarding himself as very learned. His father said to him, ‘Svetaketu, dear boy, you, I see, are conceited, arrogant, regarding yourself as very learned; did you ask for that teaching (about the Supreme Brahman) through which what is unheard becomes heard, what is unthought becomes thought of, what is unknown becomes known ?’ ‘Of what nature, revered sir, is that teaching ?’

sa: श्वेतकेतो यन् नु सोम्येदं महामना अनूचानमानी स्तब्धो ऽसि ।
उत तम् आदेशम् अप्राक्ष्यः येनाश्रुतं श्रुतं भवत्य् अमतं मतम् अविज्ञातं विज्ञातम् इति ।
कथं नु भगवः स आदेशो भवतीति ॥
iast: śvetaketo yan nu somyedaṃ mahāmanā anūcānamānī stabdho ’si ।
uta tam ādeśam aprākṣyaḥ yenāśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavaty amataṃ matam avijñātaṃ vijñātam iti ।
kathaṃ nu bhagavaḥ sa ādeśo bhavatīti ॥

tr.text: Having gone (to the teacher’s house) when twelve years old, he came back when he was twenty-four old, having studied all the Vedas, conceited, arrogant and regarding himself as very learned. His father said to him, ‘Svetaketu, dear boy, you, I see, are conceited, arrogant, regarding yourself as very learned; did you ask for that teaching (about the Supreme Brahman) through which what is unheard becomes heard, what is unthought becomes thought of, what is unknown becomes known ?’ ‘Of what nature, revered sir, is that teaching ?’

sa: यथा सोम्यैकेन मृत्पिण्डेन सर्वं मृन्मयं विज्ञातं स्यात् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं मृत्तिकेत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
iast: yathā somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛnmayaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttikety eva satyam ॥

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, just as through a single clod of clay all that is made of clay would become known, for all modifications is but name based upon words and the clay alone is real;

sa: यथा सोम्यैकेन लोहमणिना सर्वं लोहमयं विज्ञातं स्यात् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं लोहम् इत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
iast: yathā somyaikena lohamaṇinā sarvaṃ lohamayaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ loham ity eva satyam ॥

tr.text: Dear boy, just as through a single ingot of gold, all that is made of gold would become known, for all modification is but name based upon words and the gold alone is real;

sa: यथा सोम्यैकेन नखनिकृन्तनेन सर्वं कार्ष्णायसं विज्ञातं स्यात् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं कृष्णायसम् इत्य् एव सत्यम् ।
iast: yathā somyaikena nakhanikṛntanena sarvaṃ kārṣṇāyasaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ kṛṣṇāyasam ity eva satyam ।

tr.text: Dear boy, just as through a single nail-parer all that is made of iron would become known, for all modification is but name based upon words and the iron alone is real – such, dear boy, is that teaching.’

sa: न वै नूनं भगवन्तस् त एतद् अवेदिषुः ।
यद् ध्य् एतद् अवेदिष्यन् कथं मे नावक्ष्यन् ।
इति भगवांस् त्व् एव मे ब्रवीत्व् इति ।
iast: na vai nūnaṃ bhagavantas ta etad avediṣuḥ ।
yad dhy etad avediṣyan kathaṃ me nāvakṣyan ।
iti bhagavāṃs tv eva me bravītv iti ।

tr.text: ‘Surely, my revered teachers did not know it, for if they had known, why should they not have told it to me ? However, revered father, teach it to me’. ‘Be it so, dear boy’, said (the father).

sa: सद् एव सोम्येदम् अग्र आसीद् एकम् एवाद्वितीयम् ।
तद् धैक आहुर् असद् एवेदम् अग्र आसीद् एकम् एवाद्वितीयम् ।
iast: sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam ।
tad dhaika āhur asad evedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam ।

tr.text: ‘In the beginning, dear boy, this was Being alone, one only, without a second. Some say that, in the beginning, this was Non-being alone, one only, without a second. From that Non-being arose Being.’

sa: कुतस् तु खलु सोम्यैवं स्याद् इति होवाच ।
सत् त्व् एव सोम्येदम् अग्र आसीद् एकम् एवाद्वितीयम् ॥
iast: kutas tu khalu somyaivaṃ syād iti hovāca ।
sat tv eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam ॥

tr.text: Aruni said, ‘But now, indeed, dear boy, could it be so ? How could Being arise from Non-being ? In truth, dear boy, in the beginning (before creation), there was Being alone, one only, without a second.

sa: तस्माद् यत्र क्व च शोचति स्वेदते वा पुरुषस् तेजस एव तद् अध्य् आपो जायन्ते ॥
iast: tasmād yatra kva ca śocati svedate vā puruṣas tejasa eva tad adhy āpo jāyante ॥

tr.text: ‘That Being willed, "May I become many, may I grow forth." It created fire. That fire willed, "May I become many, may I grow forth". It created water. Therefore whenever a man grieves or perspires, then it is from fire that water issues.

sa: ता आप ऐक्षन्त बह्व्यः स्याम प्रजायेमहीति ता
अन्नमसृजन्त तस्माद्यत्र क्व च वर्षति तदेव भूयिष्ठमन्नं
iast: tā āpa aikṣanta bahvyaḥ syāma prajāyemahīti tā
annamasṛjanta tasmādyatra kva ca varṣati tadeva bhūyiṣṭhamannaṃ

tr.text: ‘That water willed, "May I become many, may I grow forth." It created food. Therefore wherever it rains, abundant food grows there; it is from water that food for eating is produced.

sa: तेषां खल्व् एषां भूतानां त्रीण्य् एव बीजानि भवन्त्य् आण्डजं जीवजम् उद्भिज्जम् इति ॥
iast: teṣāṃ khalv eṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ trīṇy eva bījāni bhavanty āṇḍajaṃ jīvajam udbhijjam iti ॥

tr.text: ‘Of the aforesaid beings there are only three origins: those born from eggs, born from living beings, and born from sprouts.

sa: हन्ताहम् इमास् तिस्रो देवता अनेन जीवेनात्मनानुप्रविश्य नामरूपे व्याकरवाणीति ॥
iast: hantāham imās tisro devatā anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇīti ॥

tr.text: ‘That deity willed, ‘Well, let me, entering into these three deities through this living self (Jivatman), differentiate name and form.

sa: सेयं देवतेमास् तिस्रो देवता अनेनैव जीवेनात्मनानुप्रविश्य नामरूपे व्याकरोत् ॥
iast: seyaṃ devatemās tisro devatā anenaiva jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākarot ॥

tr.text: "Of these, let me make each one triplicated", willing thus, this deity entered into these three deities through this living self and differentiated names and forms.

sa: यथा तु खलु सोम्येमास् तिस्रो देवतास् त्रिवृत् त्रिवृद् एकैका भवति तन् मे विजानीहीति ॥
iast: yathā tu khalu somyemās tisro devatās trivṛt trivṛd ekaikā bhavati tan me vijānīhīti ॥

tr.text: ‘It made each one of them threefold. But, dear boy, how each of these three deities becomes threefold (outside the body), know that from me.

sa: यद् अग्ने रोहितं रूपं तेजसस् तद् रूपम् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
iast: yad agne rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad rūpam ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇīty eva satyam ॥
words: any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: ‘In fire, the red colour is the colour of fire; that which is white belongs to water and that which is black belongs to food (earth). Thus vanishes (the idea of) the quality of fire from fire; for all modification is but name based upon words, only the three forms are real.

sa: यद् आदित्यस्य रोहितं रूपं तेजसस् तद् रूपम् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
iast: yad ādityasya rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad rūpam ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇīty eva satyam ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: ‘In the sun, the red colour is the colour of fire, that which is white belongs to water and that which is black belongs to earth. Thus vanishes (the idea of) the quality of the sun from the sun; for all modification is but name based upon words, only the three forms are real.

sa: यच् चन्द्रमसो रोहितं रूपं तेजसस् तद् रूपम् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
iast: yac candramaso rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad rūpam ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇīty eva satyam ॥
words: any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: ‘In the moon, the red colour is the colour of fire, that which is white belongs to water and that which is black belongs to earth. Thus vanishes (the idea of) the quality of the moon from the moon; for all modification is but name based upon words, only the three forms are real.

sa: यद् विद्युतो रोहितं रूपं तेजसस् तद् रूपम् ।
वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं त्रीणि रूपाणीत्य् एव सत्यम् ॥
iast: yad vidyuto rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad rūpam ।
vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇīty eva satyam ॥
words: a flashing thunderbolt (as the weapon of the Maruts)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: ‘In lightning, the red colour is the colour of fire, that which is white belongs to water and that which is black belongs to earth. Thus vanishes (the idea of) the quality of lightning from lightning; for all modification is but name based upon words, only the three forms are real.

sa: एतद् ध स्म वै तद्विद्वांस आहुः पूर्वे महाशाला महाश्रोत्रियाः ।
न नो ऽद्य कश्चनाश्रुतम् अमतम् अविज्ञातम् उदाहरिष्यति ।
iast: etad dha sma vai tadvidvāṃsa āhuḥ pūrve mahāśālā mahāśrotriyāḥ ।
na no ’dya kaścanāśrutam amatam avijñātam udāhariṣyati ।
words: being before or in front fore
a Brāhman versed in the Veda

tr.text: ‘It was indeed on knowing this (triplication) that the ancient great householders and great Vedic scholars said, ‘There is, at present, nothing that anyone would point out to us as unheard, unthought or unknown"; for from these they understood everything.

sa: यद् उ रोहितम् इवाभूद् इति तेजसस् तद् रूपम् इति तद् विदां चक्रुः ।
यद् उ शुक्लम् इवाभूद् इत्य् अपां रूपम् इति तद् विदां चक्रुः ।
यद् उ कृष्णम् इवाभूद् इत्य् अन्नस्य रूपम् इति तद् विदां चक्रुः ॥
iast: yad u rohitam ivābhūd iti tejasas tad rūpam iti tad vidāṃ cakruḥ ।
yad u śuklam ivābhūd ity apāṃ rūpam iti tad vidāṃ cakruḥ ।
yad u kṛṣṇam ivābhūd ity annasya rūpam iti tad vidāṃ cakruḥ ॥
words: the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)

tr.text: ‘Whatever else appeared red, that also they knew to be the colour of (untriplicated) fire; whatever appeared white, that also they knew to be the colour of water; whatever appeared black, that also they knew to be the colour of earth.

sa: यद् व् अविज्ञातम् इवाभूद् इत्य् एतासाम् एव देवतानां समास इति तद् विदां चक्रुः ।
यथा नु खलु सोम्येमास् तिस्रो देवताः पुरुषं प्राप्य त्रिवृत् त्रिवृद् एकैका भवति तन् मे विजानीहीति ॥
iast: yad v avijñātam ivābhūd ity etāsām eva devatānāṃ samāsa iti tad vidāṃ cakruḥ ।
yathā nu khalu somyemās tisro devatāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpya trivṛt trivṛd ekaikā bhavati tan me vijānīhīti ॥

tr.text: ‘Whatever appeared to be unknown, that also they knew to be a combination of these very deities. But, dear boy, know from me how, on reaching man, each of these three deities becomes threefold.

sa: तस्य यः स्थविष्ठो धातुस् तत् पुरीषं भवति ।
iast: tasya yaḥ sthaviṣṭho dhātus tat purīṣaṃ bhavati ।
words: (superl. of sthūra) very broad or thick or solid or strong

tr.text: ‘Food, when eaten, becomes divided into three parts. What is its grossest ingredient, that becomes faeces; what is the middling ingredient, that becomes flesh; and what is the subtlest ingredient, that becomes mind.

sa: तासां यः स्थविष्ठो धातुस् तन् मूत्रं भवति ।
iast: tāsāṃ yaḥ sthaviṣṭho dhātus tan mūtraṃ bhavati ।
words: (superl. of sthūra) very broad or thick or solid or strong
the fluid secreted by the kidneys

tr.text: ‘Water, when drunk, becomes divided into three parts. What is its grossest ingredient, that becomes urine; what is the middling ingredient, that becomes blood; and what is the subtlest ingredient, that becomes Prana.

sa: तस्य यः स्थविष्ठो धातुस् तद् अस्थि भवति ।
iast: tasya yaḥ sthaviṣṭho dhātus tad asthi bhavati ।
words: the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
(superl. of sthūra) very broad or thick or solid or strong

tr.text: ‘Fire, when eaten, becomes divided into three parts. What is its grossest ingredient, that becomes bone; what is the middling ingredient, that becomes marrow; and what is the subtlest ingredient, hat becomes speech.

sa: भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
iast: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti ।

tr.text: ‘Hence, dear boy, mind is made up of food, Prana is made up of water, and speech is made of fire. ‘Explain it further to me, revered sir’. ‘Be it so, dear boy’, said the father.

sa: दध्नः सोम्य मथ्यमानस्य यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति ।
iast: dadhnaḥ somya mathyamānasya yo ’ṇimā sa ūrdhvaḥ samudīṣati ।

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, of the curd that is being churned that which is the subtlest part rises upwards and that becomes butter.

sa: एवम् एव खलु सोम्यान्नस्याश्यमानस्य यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति ।
iast: evam eva khalu somyānnasyāśyamānasya yo ’ṇimā sa ūrdhvaḥ samudīṣati ।

tr.text: ‘So also, dear boy, of the food that is eaten that which is the subtlest part rises upwards and that becomes the mind.

sa: अपां सोम्य पीयमानानां यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति ।
iast: apāṃ somya pīyamānānāṃ yo ’ṇimā sa ūrdhvaḥ samudīṣati ।

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, of the water that is drunk that which is the subtlest part rises upwards and that becomes Prana.

sa: तेजसः सोम्याश्यमानस्य यो ऽणिमा स ऊर्ध्वः समुदीषति ।
iast: tejasaḥ somyāśyamānasya yo ’ṇimā sa ūrdhvaḥ samudīṣati ।
words: the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, of the fire that is eaten that which is the subtlest part rises upwards and that becomes speech.

sa: भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
iast: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti ।

tr.text: ‘Hence, dear boy, mind is made up of food, Prana is made up of water, and speech is made up of fire’. ‘Explain it further to me, revered sir’. ‘Be it so, dear boy’, said the father.

sa: आपोमयः प्राणो न पिबतो विच्छेत्स्यत इति ॥
iast: āpomayaḥ prāṇo na pibato vicchetsyata iti ॥
words: to cut or tear or cleave or break asunder

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, man consists of sixteen parts. Do not eat for fifteen days; drink as much water as you like. Prana is made up of water, and the Prana of one who drinks water is not cut off.

sa: अथ हैनम् उपससाद किं ब्रवीमि भो इति ।
स होवाच न वै मा प्रतिभान्ति भो इति ॥
iast: atha hainam upasasāda kiṃ bravīmi bho iti ।
sa hovāca na vai mā pratibhānti bho iti ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Svetaketu did not eat for fifteen days. Then he approached him saying, ‘What shall I say ?’ The father said, ‘The Riks, the Yajus, and the Samans, dear boy.’ ‘They do not at all arise in me, sir’.

sa: तं होवाच यथा सोम्य महतो ऽभ्याहितस्यैको ऽङ्गारः खद्योतमात्रः परिशिष्टः स्यात् ।
तेन ततो ऽपि न बहु दहेत् ।
एवं सोम्य ते षोडशानां कलानाम् एका कला अतिशिष्टा स्यात् ।
iast: taṃ hovāca yathā somya mahato ’bhyāhitasyaiko ’ṅgāraḥ khadyotamātraḥ pariśiṣṭaḥ syāt ।
evaṃ somya te ṣoḍaśānāṃ kalānām ekā kalā atiśiṣṭā syāt ।

tr.text: The father said to him, ‘Dear boy, just as a single ember of the size of a firefly, left over from a large burning fire, cannot burn any more than that, even so, dear boy, of your sixteen parts only one part is left over, now by means of that you cannot perceive the Vedas. Eat, then you will understand me’.

sa: तं ह यत् किं च पप्रच्छ सर्वं ह प्रतिपेदे ॥
iast: taṃ ha yat kiṃ ca papraccha sarvaṃ ha pratipede ॥

tr.text: He ate and then approached his father. Whatever he asked him, he answered them all.

sa: यथा सोम्य महतो ऽभ्याहितस्यैकम् अङ्गारं खद्योतमात्रं परिशिष्टं तं तृनैर् उपसमाधाय प्राज्वलयेत् तेन ततो ऽपि बहु दहेत् ॥
iast: yathā somya mahato ’bhyāhitasyaikam aṅgāraṃ khadyotamātraṃ pariśiṣṭaṃ taṃ tṛnair upasamādhāya prājvalayet tena tato ’pi bahu dahet ॥

tr.text: The father said to him, ‘Dear boy, just as when a single ember of the size of a firefly left over from a large burning fire, is made to blaze up by adding straw and it burns much more than before, even so, dear boy, of your sixteen parts, only one part remained, and that being nourished by food, has been made to blaze up; and by that you perceive the Vedas now. Hence, dear boy, the mind is made up of food, the Prana is made up of water, and speech is made up of fire. From his words, (Svetaketu) understood it – yea, he understood it.

sa: एवं सोम्य ते षोडशानां कलानाम् एका कलातिशिष्टाभूत् ।
तद् धास्य विजज्ञाव् इति विजज्ञाव् इति ॥
iast: evaṃ somya te ṣoḍaśānāṃ kalānām ekā kalātiśiṣṭābhūt ।
tad dhāsya vijajñāv iti vijajñāv iti ॥

tr.text: The father said to him, ‘Dear boy, just as when a single ember of the size of a firefly left over from a large burning fire, is made to blaze up by adding straw and it burns much more than before, even so, dear boy, of your sixteen parts, only one part remained, and that being nourished by food, has been made to blaze up; and by that you perceive the Vedas now. Hence, dear boy, the mind is made up of food, the Prana is made up of water, and speech is made up of fire. From his words, (Svetaketu) understood it – yea, he understood it.

sa: उद्दालको हारुणिः श्वेतकेतुं पुत्रम् उवाच स्वप्नान्तं मे सोम्य विजानीहीति ।
यत्रैतत् पुरुषः स्वपिति नाम सता सोम्य तदा संपन्नो भवति ।
iast: uddālako hāruṇiḥ śvetaketuṃ putram uvāca svapnāntaṃ me somya vijānīhīti ।
yatraitat puruṣaḥ svapiti nāma satā somya tadā saṃpanno bhavati ।
words: name of Uddālaka (a renowned Brāhmaṇa teacher)

tr.text: Once Uddalaka Aruni said to his son Svetaketu, ‘Dear boy, know from me the true nature of sleep. When a man is said to be sleeping, then, dear boy, he has become united with Being and has attained his own nature. Hence people speak of him as sleeping, for them he has attained his own nature.

sa: स यथा शकुनिः सूत्रेण प्रबद्धो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनम् अलब्ध्वा बन्धनम् एवोपश्रयते ।
एवम् एव खलु सोम्य तन् मनो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनम् अलब्ध्वा प्राणम् एवोपश्रयते ।
iast: sa yathā śakuniḥ sūtreṇa prabaddho diśaṃ diśaṃ patitvānyatrāyatanam alabdhvā bandhanam evopaśrayate ।
evam eva khalu somya tan mano diśaṃ diśaṃ patitvānyatrāyatanam alabdhvā prāṇam evopaśrayate ।
words: a bird (esp. a large bird = gridhra or cilla)
mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)
mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)

tr.text: ‘Just as a bird tied to a string, after flying in various directions and finding no resting place elsewhere, takes refuge at the very place where to it is tied, even so, dear boy, that mind, after flying in various directions and finding no resting place elsewhere, takes refuge in Prana alone; for the mind, dear boy, is tied to Prana.

sa: यत्रैतत् पुरुषो ऽशिशिषति नामाप एव तद् अशितं नयन्ते ।
तद् यथा गोनायो ऽश्वनायः पुरुषनाय इत्य् एवं तद् अप आचक्षते ऽशनायेति ।
iast: yatraitat puruṣo ’śiśiṣati nāmāpa eva tad aśitaṃ nayante ।
tad yathā gonāyo ’śvanāyaḥ puruṣanāya ity evaṃ tad apa ācakṣate ’śanāyeti ।
words: the sheath or calyx of a bud

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, know from me (the true nature of) hunger and thirst. When a man is said to be hungry, then (it is to be understood that), water is leading away what has been eaten; (therefore water may be designated as hunger). Just as people speak of the leader of cows, the leader of horses, and the leader of men, even so they speak of water as the leader of food. Hence, dear boy, know this shoot (the body) to be put forth (by a root), for it cannot be without a root.

sa: एवम् एव खलु सोम्यान्नेन शुङ्गेनापो मूलम् अन्विच्छ ।
अद्भिः सोम्य शुङ्गेन तेजो मूलम् अन्विच्छ ।
सन्मूलाः सोम्येमाः सर्वाः प्रजाः सदायतनाः सत्प्रतिष्ठाः ॥
iast: evam eva khalu somyānnena śuṅgenāpo mūlam anviccha ।
adbhiḥ somya śuṅgena tejo mūlam anviccha ।
sanmūlāḥ somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sadāyatanāḥ satpratiṣṭhāḥ ॥
words: where? in what place? whither?(sometimes connected with particles ﾮMDBOﾯ~ṝha)
a root (of any plant or tree)
the sheath or calyx of a bud
a root (of any plant or tree)

tr.text: ‘Where could its root be apart from food ? Even so, dear boy, with food as the shoot, look for water as the root; with water as the shoot, dear boy, look for fire as the root; with fire as the shoot, dear boy, look for Being as the root. All these creatures, dear boy, have Being as their root, have Being as their abode, and have Being as their support.

sa: अथ यत्रैतत् पुरुषः पिपासति नाम तेज एव तत् पीतं नयते ।
तद् यथा गोनायो ऽश्वनायः पुरुषनाय इत्य् एवं तत् तेज आचष्ट उदन्येति ।
तत्रैतद् एव शुङ्गम् उत्पतितं सोम्य विजानीहि ।
iast: atha yatraitat puruṣaḥ pipāsati nāma teja eva tat pītaṃ nayate ।
tad yathā gonāyo ’śvanāyaḥ puruṣanāya ity evaṃ tat teja ācaṣṭa udanyeti ।
tatraitad eva śuṅgam utpatitaṃ somya vijānīhi ।
words: the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
the sharp edge (of a knife etc.)
the sheath or calyx of a bud

tr.text: ‘Again, when a man is said to be thirsty, then (it is to be understood that), fire is leading away what has been drunk: (therefore fire may be designated as thirst). Just as people speak of the leader of cows, the leader of horses, and the leader of men, even so they speak of that fire as the leader of water. Hence, dear boy, know this shoot (water) to be put forth (by a root), for it cannot be without a root.

sa: अद्भिः सोम्य शुङ्गेन तेजो मूलम् अन्विच्छ ।
सन्मूलाः सोम्येमाः सर्वाः प्रजाः सद् आयतनाः सत्प्रतिष्ठाः ।
यथा नु खलु सोम्येमास् तिस्रो देवताः पुरुषं प्राप्य त्रिवृत् त्रिवृद् एकैका भवति तद् उक्तं पुरस्ताद् एव भवति ।
अस्य सोम्य पुरुषस्य प्रयतो वाङ् मनसि संपद्यते मनः प्राणे प्राणस् तेजसि तेजः परस्यां देवतायाम् ॥
iast: adbhiḥ somya śuṅgena tejo mūlam anviccha ।
sanmūlāḥ somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sad āyatanāḥ satpratiṣṭhāḥ ।
yathā nu khalu somyemās tisro devatāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpya trivṛt trivṛd ekaikā bhavati tad uktaṃ purastād eva bhavati ।
asya somya puruṣasya prayato vāṅ manasi saṃpadyate manaḥ prāṇe prāṇas tejasi tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyām ॥
words: where? in what place? whither?(sometimes connected with particles ﾮMDBOﾯ~ṝha)

tr.text: ‘Where could its root be apart from water ? Dear boy, with water as the shoot, look for fire as the root; with fire as the shoot, look for Being as the root. All these creatures, dear boy, have Being as their root, have Being as their abode, and have Being as their support. How dear boy, each of these three deities, on reaching man, becomes threefold has been explained to you earlier. When this man is about to depart, dear boy, his speech merges in the mind, mind in Prana, Prana in fire and fire in the supreme deity.

sa: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
iast: sa ya eṣo ’ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam ।
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti ।

tr.text: ‘That Being which is this subtle essence (cause), even That all this world has for its self. That is the true. That is the Atman. That thou art, O Svetaketu.’ ‘Revered sir, please explain it further to me’. ‘So be it, dear boy’, said (the father).

sa: यथा सोम्य मधु मधुकृतो निस्तिष्ठन्ति नानात्ययानां वृक्षाणां रसान् समवहारम् एकतां रसं गमयन्ति ॥
iast: yathā somya madhu madhukṛto nistiṣṭhanti nānātyayānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ rasān samavahāram ekatāṃ rasaṃ gamayanti ॥
words: the sap or juice of plants
the sap or juice of plants

tr.text: ‘As, dear boy, the bees make honey by collecting juices from different trees and reduce them into one essence, and there, as these juices have no such discrimination as "I am the juice of this tree, I am the juice of that tree"; even so, dear boy, all these creatures having merged into Being, do not know, "We have merged into Being."

sa: ते यथा तत्र न विवेकं लभन्ते ऽमुष्याहं वृक्षस्य रसो ऽस्म्य् अमुष्याहं वृक्षस्य रसो ऽस्मीति ।
एवम् एव खलु सोम्येमाः सर्वाः प्रजाः सति संपद्य न विदुः सति संपद्यामह इति ॥
iast: te yathā tatra na vivekaṃ labhante ’muṣyāhaṃ vṛkṣasya raso ’smy amuṣyāhaṃ vṛkṣasya raso ’smīti ।
evam eva khalu somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sati saṃpadya na viduḥ sati saṃpadyāmaha iti ॥
words: the sap or juice of plants
the sap or juice of plants

tr.text: ‘As, dear boy, the bees make honey by collecting juices from different trees and reduce them into one essence, and there, as these juices have no such discrimination as "I am the juice of this tree, I am the juice of that tree"; even so, dear boy, all these creatures having merged into Being, do not know, "We have merged into Being."

sa: त इह व्यघ्रो वा सिंहो वा वृको वा वराहो वा कीटो वा पतङ्गो वा दंशो वा मशको वा यद् यद् भवन्ति तद् आभवन्ति ॥
iast: ta iha vyaghro vā siṃho vā vṛko vā varāho vā kīṭo vā pataṅgo vā daṃśo vā maśako vā yad yad bhavanti tad ābhavanti ॥

tr.text: ‘Whatever these creatures are here, tiger or lion or wolf or boar or worm or flying insect or gad-fly or mosquito, that they become again.

sa: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
iast: sa ya eṣo ’ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam ।
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti ।

tr.text: ‘That Being which is this subtle essence (cause), even That all this world has for its self. That is the true. That is the Atman. That thou art, O Svetaketu.’ ‘Revered sir, please explain it further to me’. ‘So be it, dear boy’, said (the father).

sa: इमाः सोम्य नद्यः पुरस्तात् प्राच्यः स्यन्दन्ते पश्चात् प्रतीच्यः ।
ता यथा तत्र न विदुर् इयम् अहम् अस्मीयम् अहम् अस्मीति ॥
iast: imāḥ somya nadyaḥ purastāt prācyaḥ syandante paścāt pratīcyaḥ ।
tā yathā tatra na vidur iyam aham asmīyam aham asmīti ॥

tr.text: ‘These eastern rivers, dear boy, flow along to the east and the western ones to the west. They rise from the ocean and merge in the ocean, and become that ocean itself. And there as these rivers do not know themselves as "I am this river, I am that river", even so, dear boy, all these creatures, having come from Being, do not know, "We have come from Being". And whatever these creatures were here, tiger or lion or wolf or boar or worm or flying insect or gad-fly or mosquito, that they become again.

sa: एवम् एव खलु सोम्येमाः सर्वाः प्रजाः सत आगम्य न विदुः सत आगच्छामह इति ।
त इह व्याघ्रो वा सिंहो वा वृको वा वराहो वा कीटो वा पतङ्गो वा दंशो वा मशको वा यद् यद् भवन्ति तद् आभवन्ति ॥
iast: evam eva khalu somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sata āgamya na viduḥ sata āgacchāmaha iti ।
ta iha vyāghro vā siṃho vā vṛko vā varāho vā kīṭo vā pataṅgo vā daṃśo vā maśako vā yad yad bhavanti tad ābhavanti ॥
words: to be present or near at hand

tr.text: ‘These eastern rivers, dear boy, flow along to the east and the western ones to the west. They rise from the ocean and merge in the ocean, and become that ocean itself. And there as these rivers do not know themselves as "I am this river, I am that river", even so, dear boy, all these creatures, having come from Being, do not know, "We have come from Being". And whatever these creatures were here, tiger or lion or wolf or boar or worm or flying insect or gad-fly or mosquito, that they become again.

भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
iast: sa ya eṣo ’ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam ।
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti ।

tr.text: ‘That Being which is this subtle essence (cause), even That all this world has for its self. That is the true. That is the Atman. That thou art, O Svetaketu.’ ‘Revered sir, please explain it further to me’. ‘So be it, dear boy’, said (the father).

sa: अस्य सोम्य महतो वृक्षस्य यो मूले ऽभ्याहन्याज् जीवन् स्रवेद् यो मध्ये ऽभ्याहन्याज् जीवन् स्रवेद् यो ऽग्रे ऽभ्याहन्याज् जीवन् स्रवेत् ।
स एष जीवेनात्मनानुप्रभूतः पेपीयमानो मोदमानस् तिष्ठति ॥
iast: asya somya mahato vṛkṣasya yo mūle ’bhyāhanyāj jīvan sraved yo madhye ’bhyāhanyāj jīvan sraved yo ’gre ’bhyāhanyāj jīvan sravet ।
sa eṣa jīvenātmanānuprabhūtaḥ pepīyamāno modamānas tiṣṭhati ॥
words: a root (of any plant or tree)
to be merry or glad or happy

tr.text: ‘Of this large tree, dear boy, if anyone were to strike at the root, it would exude sap, though still living; if anyone were to strike in the middle, it would exude sap, though still living; if anyone were to strike at the top, it would exude sap, though still living. As that tree is pervaded by the living self, it stands firm, drinking constantly and rejoicing.

sa: अस्य यद् एकां शाखां जीवो जहात्य् अथ सा शुष्यति ।
iast: asya yad ekāṃ śākhāṃ jīvo jahāty atha sā śuṣyati ।
words: forming the 2nd part or half of anything

tr.text: ‘If the life leaves one branch of this tree, then that branch dries up; if it leaves the second one, then that dries up; it leaves the whole tree, the whole tree dries up.’

sa: एवम् एव खलु सोम्य विद्धीति ह उवाच ।
जीवापेतं वाव किलेदं म्रियते न जीवो म्रियत इति ।
स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।
iast: evam eva khalu somya viddhīti ha uvāca ।
jīvāpetaṃ vāva kiledaṃ mriyate na jīvo mriyata iti ।
sa ya eṣo ’ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam ।
bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti ।

tr.text: The father said, ‘Dear boy, know that even so, being left by the living self this body surely dies, but the living self does not die. That Being which is this subtle essence (cause), even That all this world has for its self. That is the true. That is the Atman. That thou art, O Svetaketu.’ ‘Revered sir, please explain it further to me’. ‘So be it, dear boy’, said (the father).

‘Bring a fruit from this Banyan tree’. ‘Here it is, revered sir’. ‘Break it.’ ‘It is broken, revered sir’. ‘What do you see in this ?’ ‘These seeds, small like particles, revered sir’. ‘Break one of these, my child’. ‘It is broken, revered sir’. ‘What do you see in it ?’ ‘Nothing, revered sir’.

sa: तं होवाच यं वै सोम्यैतम् अणिमानं न निभालयस एतस्य वै सोम्यैषो ऽणिम्न एवं महान्यग्रोधस् तिष्ठति ।
iast: taṃ hovāca yaṃ vai somyaitam aṇimānaṃ na nibhālayasa etasya vai somyaiṣo ’ṇimna evaṃ mahānyagrodhas tiṣṭhati ।

tr.text: The father said to him, ‘Dear boy, this subtle essence which you do not perceive, growing from this subtle essence the large Banyan tree thus stands. Have faith, dear boy.’

sa: स य एषो ऽणिमैतद् आत्म्यम् इदं सर्वम् ।
भूय एव मा भगवान् विज्ञापयत्व् इति ।

bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti ।

sa: लवणम् एतद् उदके ऽवधायाथ मा प्रातर् उपसीदथा इति ।
यद् दोषा लवणम् उदके ऽवाधा अङ्ग तद् आहरेति ।
iast: lavaṇam etad udake ’vadhāyātha mā prātar upasīdathā iti ।
yad doṣā lavaṇam udake ’vādhā aṅga tad āhareti ।

tr.text: ‘Put this salt into water and then come to me in the morning’. He did so. The father said to him, ‘Bring the salt, my child, which you put into water at night’. Having searched for it, he did not find it, as it has completely dissolved. ‘My child, take a sip from the top of this water. How is it?’ ‘It is salt’. ‘Take a sip from the middle. How is it ?’ ‘It is salt’. ‘Take a sip from the bottom. How is it ?’ ‘It is salt’. ‘Throw this water away and then come to me’. He did so (and returned saying), ‘It is there always’. The father said to him, ‘Dear boy, as you do not see what is present in this water though indeed it exists in it, similarly, (Being exists) indeed in this body.

sa: तं होवाचात्र वाव किल तत् सोम्य न निभालयसे ऽत्रैव किलेति ॥
iast: taṃ hovācātra vāva kila tat somya na nibhālayase ’traiva kileti ॥
words: (a particle of asseveration or emphasis) indeed
